About Wood Contracting Inc

Wood Contracting Inc is a  licensed (TGC105501) and insured Chicago home remodeling company specializing in kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, and whole home renovations for condos, townhomes, and single-family residences throughout Chicago and the surrounding suburbs.

Owner Dillon Wood personally oversees every residential remodeling project, ensuring quality control and direct communication from initial consultation through final walkthrough. Our owner-operated approach means dedicated tradespeople complete your kitchen renovation or bathroom remodel, delivering the craftsmanship and attention to detail that larger remodeling companies cannot provide.

We serve Chicago neighborhoods, including Lincoln Park, South Loop, West Loop, Logan Square, Wicker Park, Old Town, Bucktown, Lakeview, and surrounding areas. Whether you're planning a complete home renovation or a focused kitchen or bathroom remodel, Wood Contracting delivers transparent pricing, realistic timelines, and superior results.

Frequently Asked Questions About Chicago Home Remodeling

Get answers to common questions about kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, timelines, costs, and what to expect during your residential remodeling project.

How Long Does A Typical Bathroom Or Kitchen Remodel Take?

Most bathroom renovations take 2-5 weeks from demolition to completion. Kitchen remodeling typically requires 4-6 weeks. Whole home renovations vary based on scope but generally range from 6-12 weeks. We provide detailed timelines during your free consultation and work diligently to meet deadlines.

How Much Does A Home Remodeling Project Cost In Chicago?

Project costs vary significantly based on scope, size, and material selections. Bathroom remodels typically range from $12,000-$55,000+. Kitchen renovations generally cost $15,000-$80,000+. Whole home remodeling projects vary widely based on square footage and complexity. Wood Contracting delivers superior value without showroom overhead or sales commissions. We provide transparent, detailed proposals during your free consultation.

Do You Handle Permits And HOA Approvals?

Absolutely. We manage all permit applications, HOA submissions, and compliance requirements. With decades of experience navigating Chicago building codes and downtown condo associations, we handle the administrative work so you don't have to. We're familiar with requirements across all Chicago neighborhoods and building types.

What's Included In Your Workmanship Warranty?

Every Wood Contracting project comes with a 1-year workmanship warranty covering our installation and construction. We stand behind our work and ensure you're completely satisfied with the finished results. Material warranties are provided by manufacturers.

What Makes Wood Contracting Different From Other Chicago Contractors?

We're owner-operated, which means Dillon Wood and our dedicated team complete your project, not subcontractors. With 500+ completed projects and an 90% referral rate, we've built our reputation on quality craftsmanship and transparent pricing. We don't have expensive showroom overhead, so your investment goes into your home, not our retail space.

What Areas Of Chicago Do You Serve?

We primarily serve downtown Chicago neighborhoods including South Loop, West Loop, Lincoln Park, Logan Square, Wicker Park, Old Town, Bucktown, and surrounding areas. Our service area extends throughout Cook County from Hyde Park to Evanston. If your home is outside these areas, contact us to discuss your project.

Can I Stay In My Home During The Remodeling?

Yes, most clients remain in their homes during remodeling projects. We contain dust, protect your space, clean up daily, and work respectfully in your home. While some disruption is unavoidable, particularly during kitchen remodels, we minimize inconvenience wherever possible.

Do You Provide Design Services?

We partner with multiple experienced designers, including Emily Andersson Design. Alternatively, you can work with your own designer, or we can help you select materials and finishes without formal design services. We're flexible to match your needs and budget.

Are You Licensed And Insured?

Yes, Wood Contracting is fully licensed and insured. We also meet or exceed all building and HOA requirements. We carry comprehensive liability insurance and workers' compensation coverage to protect you and our team throughout your project.

What If We Encounter Unexpected Issues During Construction?

Surprises occasionally happen, especially in older Chicago buildings. Hidden water damage, outdated wiring, or structural issues sometimes appear during demolition. We address problems immediately, explain your options clearly, and provide transparent pricing for necessary repairs. No hidden fees or surprise charges.

How Does Wood Contracting's Remodeling Process Work?

Our streamlined Chicago home remodeling process takes you from initial consultation to final walkthrough with clear communication at every step.

1. Free Estimate

We'll do a site visit to see your space, take measurements, and walk you through your options with a free, no-commitment estimate.

2. Proposal

You'll get a clear, itemized proposal that breaks down the full scope of work, timeline, and costs to get a straightforward look at exactly what you're getting.

3. Design Selection

Work with our team or your designer to select materials, finishes, and fixtures. We'll handle permits, your HOA, and any building coordination.

4. Build

Our dedicated team completes your project with careful attention to detail. Dillon or your project manager communicates throughout and ensures quality at every stage.

5. Final Review

We review every detail together and address any items immediately. Your project is backed by our 1-year workmanship warranty.

Your kitchen should work for how you live. Whether you're dealing with a cramped condo galley, an outdated townhome layout that kills conversation, or a single-family kitchen stuck in 1995, we transform Chicago kitchens into spaces that actually function and look great.

Custom Kitchen Cabinets That Maximize Every Inch

Chicago kitchens rarely have space to waste. Generic cabinets leave gaps along walls, create dead corners with spinning lazy Susans that hold three items, and force you to work around standard heights that don't match how you cook. Custom kitchen cabinets solve these frustrations by fitting your exact space and how you actually use your kitchen.

The Wood Contracting team specializes in custom kitchen cabinets Chicago. We design cabinets that reach the ceiling for maximum storage, create corner solutions that actually access deep space, build in appliance garages and charging stations, incorporate pull-out organizers for pots and spices, and design around your specific appliances and workflow.

Transform your kitchen with cabinets designed for your space, your cooking style, and your storage needs instead of fighting with one-size-fits-none solutions.

Historic Home Kitchens: Modernizing With Character

Lincoln Park, Bucktown, Old Town, Logan Square kitchen remodeling requires balancing preservation with modernization. These neighborhoods feature beautiful vintage homes with kitchens that need serious updating. Original layouts designed for different cooking styles. Outdated electrical and plumbing. Details worth preserving are mixed with a function that no longer works.

We balance respect for architectural character with modern functionality. Updated systems that meet current codes. Layouts reconfigured for how people actually cook today. Storage solutions that didn't exist when your home was built.

What makes this work: Understanding which walls are structural. Knowing Chicago building codes inside and out. Experience with old plumbing and electrical systems. Appreciation for original details worth keeping. Skill to blend old and new seamlessly.

High-End Kitchen Remodeling Chicago: When Quality Matters Most

Some homeowners want a luxury kitchen remodel with every detail elevated: custom cabinetry built to exact specifications, premium natural stone countertops like granite or quartz, intricate tile backsplashes that become focal points, professional-grade appliances from brands like Wolf or Sub-Zero, hardwood or specialty flooring, custom lighting design, and built-in storage solutions.

Wood Contracting's Chicago kitchen remodeling team excels at high-end installations that require precision craftsmanship. We handle custom range hoods, integrated appliance installations, designer hardware, decorative tile patterns, crown molding, and architectural trim details that transform your kitchen into a showpiece.

Our luxury kitchen remodels stand out through meticulous execution: perfect tile cuts around outlets and edges, custom cabinetry that fits seamlessly, countertop seams that disappear, precisely aligned hardware, and factory-quality paint and finish work.

Our Kitchen Remodeling Chicago Process

Kitchen remodeling Chicago transforms outdated, cramped, or dysfunctional kitchens into spaces you'll love cooking in and gathering around. Our kitchen remodeling process handles everything from layout changes to custom cabinetry installation, completing most Chicago kitchen remodels in 4-6 weeks with quality that lasts.

In-Home Consultation

We begin your kitchen remodeling Chicago project with an in-home consultation to understand how you cook and use your kitchen, discuss layout frustrations and what's not working, review your style preferences and inspiration images, assess structural considerations and possibilities, and establish realistic budget and timeline for your kitchen renovation Chicago.

Design & Material Selection

Our kitchen remodeling team works with you or your designer to finalize layouts that improve workflow and storage, select cabinetry style and configuration, choose countertops and backsplash tile, plan lighting and electrical upgrades, and coordinate appliance selections. We design Chicago kitchens that balance beauty with serious functionality.

Procurement & Prep

Once your kitchen remodeling Chicago design is approved, we order custom cabinetry to your exact specifications, schedule countertop fabrication and installation, procure tile and all finish materials, coordinate plumbing and electrical materials, and prepare your home for the construction phase of your kitchen renovation.

Demo & Structural Work

Our team carefully removes your existing kitchen while protecting adjacent rooms from dust and debris, addresses any structural changes or wall removal, updates plumbing and electrical rough-in, installs new gas lines if needed, and ensures the space is properly prepared for your new Chicago kitchen installation.

Cabinet & Finish Installation

During kitchen remodeling, we install custom cabinetry with precision, fabricate and install countertops, complete all backsplash tile work, install new flooring if included, add lighting fixtures and hardware, and ensure every detail reflects the quality craftsmanship your Chicago kitchen renovation deserves.

Final Details & Closeout

We complete your Chicago kitchen remodel with final paint and touch-ups, thorough cleaning and debris removal, appliance installation if we're handling it, testing all systems and functions, and a detailed walkthrough where we ensure you're absolutely thrilled with your transformed kitchen and ready to start cooking.

What Makes Wood Contracting Chicago Kitchen Remodeling Different?
Learn More About Us
Custom Tile Work That Becomes The Focal Point

Tile can make or break a kitchen. We specialize in custom backsplash installations that elevate the entire space: intricate patterns and mosaics, large-format porcelain with minimal grout lines, natural stone installations, glass and metal accents, and precise cuts around windows, outlets, and edges.

Our tile work gets noticed. It's the difference between a nice kitchen and one that makes people stop and look.

Finish Carpentry And Attention To Detail

A well-built kitchen is defined long before the final coat of paint. It’s in the precision of the carpentry behind it. Clean lines, tight reveals, and seamless transitions between surfaces create a space that feels intentional and refined. Every joint is measured, cut, and installed to disappear into the design.

We treat finish carpentry as the foundation of a high-end kitchen, not an afterthought.

‍

Smart Solutions For Chicago's Challenging Spaces

Chicago kitchens rarely come easy. Small footprints, structural limitations, old building quirks, HOA restrictions - we've seen it all and know how to navigate it.

Common challenges we solve: Maximizing storage in compact condo kitchens. Working around structural columns or soffits. Bringing old plumbing and electrical up to code. Improving lighting in kitchens with limited natural light. Creating better flow in awkward layouts. Fitting modern appliances into historic spaces. Meeting building and HOA requirements for condos. Coordinating work in occupied buildings.

Understanding What Works In Chicago Kitchen Remodeling

We've completed kitchen remodeling in South Loop high-rises, West Loop lofts, Lincoln Park greystones, Wicker Park vintage buildings, Bucktown single-families, Old Town townhomes. Each neighborhood, each building type, each era brings different considerations for kitchen renovation.

You're not getting a contractor learning on your project. You're getting a team that's done this repeatedly in spaces like yours.

The size of your space, the materials you select, and the extent of the remodel all factor into the cost. Final pricing depends on finishes, layout changes, and building requirements. Frequently Asked Questions About Kitchen Remodeling In Chicago

See the commonly asked questions Chicago homeowners ask when exploring a kitchen remodel.

How Long Will I Be Without A Kitchen During Remodeling?

Most complete kitchen remodels take 4-6 weeks from demolition to completion. During this time, your kitchen won't be fully functional. We recommend setting up a temporary kitchen in another room with a microwave, coffee maker, mini fridge, and toaster. Many clients embrace exploring Chicago's restaurant scene during remodels. We work efficiently to minimize disruption and get you back to cooking as quickly as possible.

Can I Stay In My Home During Kitchen Remodeling?

Absolutely. Most clients remain in their homes during kitchen remodels. We contain dust with plastic barriers, protect your floors and adjacent spaces, and clean up thoroughly at the end of each day. While it's not always convenient to live without a functional kitchen for several weeks, it's definitely manageable. We respect that this is your home and work carefully to minimize disruption.

How Much Does Kitchen Remodeling Cost In Chicago?

Kitchen remodeling costs in Chicago typically range from $15,000 for cosmetic updates to $80,000+ for complete gut remodels with high-end finishes. The main cost factors are cabinetry (30-40% of budget), labor for all trades, countertops and backsplash, appliances (if we're installing them), and flooring. A typical mid-range kitchen remodel in Chicago costs $22,000-$50,000. We provide detailed, transparent proposals so you understand exactly where your investment goes.

Do You Provide Kitchen Design Services?

We partner with two exceptional local interior designers. Both have extensive experience designing Chicago kitchens for every style and budget. Alternatively, you can work with your own designer, or we can help you select materials and finishes without formal design services. We're flexible to match your needs and preferences.

What If You Encounter Unexpected Issues During Demolition?

Opening walls sometimes reveals surprises common in older Chicago buildings: hidden water damage, outdated wiring not meeting current code, or structural issues. We document everything immediately, explain your options clearly, and provide transparent pricing for necessary repairs before proceeding. While unexpected issues can add cost and time, we handle them professionally and keep you informed throughout.

Can You Work With My Existing Appliances?

Yes, if your appliances are in good condition and will work with your new kitchen design, we can integrate them. However, kitchen remodeling is often an ideal time to upgrade appliances since plumbing and electrical are already being updated. If you're planning to replace appliances within 3-5 years anyway, it often makes sense to do it during the remodel.

Do You Handle Permits For Kitchen Remodeling?

We never ask for full payment upfront, and we don't request final payment until you're completely satisfied with the work.

Yes, we frequently handle open concept conversions that remove walls between kitchens and adjacent rooms. These projects require careful structural planning to ensure proper support. Many Chicago condos and older homes have cramped bathrooms that feel more like closets than retreats. Limited floor space, awkward layouts, and minimal storage make mornings frustrating instead of refreshing. We transform small bathrooms into efficient, beautiful spaces that feel significantly larger.

The Wood Contracting team specializes in small bathroom optimization. We reconfigure layouts to maximize usable space, install wall-mounted vanities to open up floor area, design custom tile patterns that visually expand the room, and create clever storage solutions that keep everything organized.

Transform your cramped bathroom into a spa-like retreat where every inch works beautifully, no matter how tight the footprint.

High-End Bathroom Renovation Chicago: Luxury That Lasts

Some homeowners want a luxury bathroom remodel with every detail elevated: custom tile installations from floor to ceiling, premium natural stone like marble or quartzite, frameless glass shower enclosures, freestanding soaking tubs, heated flooring systems, designer fixtures from brands like Kohler or Brizo, custom vanities with sophisticated storage, and integrated lighting design.

Wood Contracting's Chicago bathroom renovation team excels at high-end installations that require precision craftsmanship. We handle complex tile patterns, waterfall countertop edges, perfectly aligned tile seams, custom shower niches, body sprays and rain heads, floating vanities, and architectural details that transform your bathroom into a personal sanctuary.

Our luxury bathroom remodels stand out through meticulous execution: perfectly level tile throughout, seamless corners and transitions, flawless grout lines, precisely installed fixtures, custom storage solutions, and factory-quality finish work that rivals the finest hotels.

Historic Home Bathrooms: Updating With Respect For Character

Lincoln Park, Bucktown, Old Town, Logan Square bathroom remodeling requires balancing preservation with modernization. These neighborhoods feature beautiful vintage homes with bathrooms that desperately need updating. Original plumbing that's decades past its lifespan. Outdated electrical systems. Tiny spaces designed before modern fixtures existed. Beautiful details worth preserving mixed with layouts that no longer function.

We balance respect for architectural character with modern comfort and functionality. Updated plumbing and electrical that meet current codes. Layouts reconfigured for contemporary fixtures and storage. Modern waterproofing behind period-appropriate finishes.

What makes this work: Understanding old building construction methods. Knowing Chicago building codes inside and out. Experience with vintage plumbing and electrical systems. Appreciation for original tile, fixtures, or details worth restoring. Skill to blend period charm with modern performance seamlessly.

Condo Bathroom Remodeling Chicago: Navigating Building Requirements

Downtown Chicago condos present unique challenges for bathroom remodeling. Strict building requirements, HOA approvals, plumbing restrictions, waterproofing standards, and coordination for water shutoffs. We've completed dozens of condo bathroom remodeling projects from River North to Gold Coast, and we know exactly how to navigate building requirements while delivering beautiful results.

What we do differently: Proper waterproofing systems that meet or exceed building standards, protecting units below. Custom tile work designed for your exact space, maximizing visual impact. Premium fixtures selected to fit condo plumbing configurations. Ventilation solutions that comply with building codes. Layouts optimized for small footprints common in high-rise units.

We handle all HOA submissions, building coordination, elevator reservations, and work hour restrictions. You get a bathroom that meets every requirement while exceeding your expectations for quality and design.

We created a modern bathroom design that balances clean lines with natural textures. Vertical wood-look tile was used to visually increase height and add warmth, while green herringbone tile introduced contrast and character in the shower and custom niche. A floating vanity, integrated tub ledge, arched mirrors, and streamlined plumbing fixtures deliver a cohesive and functional design. Materials were selected for durability, easy maintenance, and timeless appeal.

The completed bathroom is a bright, modern, and highly functional space that fits seamlessly into this South Loop townhome. The remodel improved daily usability while creating a spa-like feel and increasing home value. This project highlights our expertise in Chicago townhome renovations and high-end bathroom remodeling.

Our Bathroom Remodeling Chicago Process

Bathroom remodeling Chicago creates functional, beautiful bathrooms in everything from cramped condo spaces to vintage home layouts. Our bathroom renovation process handles custom tile work, plumbing updates, and condo building requirements to transform your Chicago bathroom in 3-5 weeks.

Initial Consultation

We start your bathroom remodeling Chicago project with an in-home consultation to discuss your vision and frustrations with the current space, take precise measurements of your bathroom, review plumbing and layout options, establish budget and timeline, and for condos, discuss building requirements and HOA coordination.

Design & Material Selection

Our bathroom renovation Chicago team creates a detailed design showing tile layouts and patterns, vanity and fixture placement, lighting and electrical plans, storage solutions, and presents material options for tile, countertops, and finishes. We design bathrooms that maximize every inch of your Chicago space.

Permits & Code Coordination

Bathroom remodeling in Chicago requires permits for plumbing and electrical work. We handle all permit applications, submit required documentation to your condo building or HOA if applicable, coordinate water shutoffs with building management, and ensure your bathroom renovation meets all Chicago building codes.

Demo & Prep

Our team carefully removes your existing bathroom fixtures, tile, and finishes, protects your home from dust and debris, removes all materials from the premises, addresses any plumbing or structural issues discovered, and prepares surfaces for waterproofing and new installation.

Tile Installation & Fixtures

During bathroom remodeling Chicago, we install proper waterproofing systems, complete all custom tile work on floors and walls, install new plumbing fixtures and vanity, add lighting and ventilation, and ensure every detail meets our quality standards and your expectations for your renovated bathroom.

Final Details & Walkthrough

We finish your bathroom renovation with final paint and caulk work, hardware and accessory installation, thorough cleaning, and a detailed walkthrough. We ensure your bathroom remodeling Chicago project is complete and you love using your transformed space every single day.

What Makes Wood Contracting Chicago Bathroom Remodeling Different?

Custom Tile Work That Defines The Space

Tile work makes or breaks a bathroom. We specialize in custom installations that elevate the entire space: floor-to-ceiling shower tile in intricate patterns, large-format porcelain with precision alignment, natural stone installations like marble or travertine, accent walls and feature strips, and flawless cuts around niches, fixtures, and edges.

Our tile work gets noticed. It's the difference between a standard bathroom renovation and one that looks professionally designed and expertly executed.

Smart Solutions For Chicago's Challenging Bathroom Spaces

Chicago bathrooms rarely come easy. Tight footprints, old plumbing stacks, building restrictions, moisture issues - we've seen it all and know how to navigate it.

Common challenges we solve: Maximizing storage in compact condo bathrooms. Working around structural limitations or plumbing stacks. Bringing old plumbing and electrical up to code. Improving ventilation in windowless bathrooms. Creating better layouts in awkward configurations. Fitting modern fixtures into vintage spaces. Meeting waterproofing requirements for condos. Coordinating water shutoffs in occupied buildings.

Understanding What Works In Chicago Bathroom Remodeling

We've completed bathroom remodeling in South Loop high-rises, West Loop lofts, Lincoln Park greystones, Wicker Park vintage buildings, Bucktown single-families, Old Town townhomes. Each neighborhood, each building type, each era brings different considerations for bathroom renovation.

You're not getting a contractor learning on your project. You're getting a team that's done this repeatedly in spaces like yours.

A well-built kitchen is defined long before the final coat of paint. It’s in the precision of the carpentry behind it. Clean lines, tight reveals, and seamless transitions between surfaces create a space that feels intentional and refined. Every joint is measured, cut, and installed to disappear into the design.

We treat finish carpentry as the foundation of a high-end kitchen, not an afterthought.

Frequently Asked Questions About Bathroom Remodeling In Chicago

See the commonly asked questions Chicago homeowners ask when exploring a bathroom remodel.

How Long Does Bathroom Remodeling Take?

Most complete bathroom remodels take 2-5 weeks from demolition to completion. Small powder rooms or half baths can be completed in 2-3 weeks, while full primary bathrooms with extensive tile work take 4-5 weeks. The timeline depends on the scope of work, complexity of tile design, any plumbing relocation, and whether we're dealing with unexpected issues common in older Chicago buildings. We provide a detailed timeline in your proposal.

Can I Use My Bathroom During Remodeling?

If you're remodeling your only bathroom, you won't have access to it for 2-4 weeks. We recommend arranging alternative arrangements with neighbors, family, or a nearby gym. If you have multiple bathrooms, we can phase the work to ensure you always have at least one functional bathroom. Many Chicago homeowners with one bathroom choose to time their remodel around a vacation or stay elsewhere temporarily.

How Much Does Bathroom Remodeling Cost In Chicago?

Bathroom remodeling costs in Chicago typically range from $12,000 for basic updates to $55,000+ for luxury primary bathroom remodels. The main cost factors are tile work (both materials and skilled labor), plumbing fixtures and relocation, vanity and countertop, custom shower or tub installation, and any necessary structural or plumbing updates. A typical full bathroom remodel in Chicago costs $18,000-$30,000. We provide detailed, transparent proposals so you understand exactly where your investment goes.

Do You Provide Bathroom Design Services?

We partner with two exceptional local interior designers who specialize in Chicago bathroom design. Both have extensive experience creating functional, beautiful bathrooms for every style and budget. Alternatively, you can work with your own designer, or we can help you select materials and create a layout without formal design services. We're flexible to match your needs and preferences.

What Unexpected Issues Might You Find During Demolition?

Opening walls in Chicago bathrooms often reveals surprises: hidden water damage behind tile, outdated plumbing not meeting current code, mold from moisture issues, or structural problems. We document everything immediately with photos, explain your options clearly, and provide transparent pricing for necessary repairs before proceeding. While unexpected issues can add cost and time, we handle them professionally and keep you informed throughout.

Can You Relocate Plumbing Fixtures In My Bathroom?

Yes, we regularly relocate toilets, vanities, and showers to improve bathroom layouts. However, plumbing relocation adds both cost and time to your project. It requires opening walls and floors, rerouting supply and drain lines, and potentially updating venting. In condos, there may be building restrictions on plumbing relocation. We evaluate what's possible in your space and provide clear pricing for any plumbing changes.

Do You Handle Permits For Bathroom Remodeling?

When permits are required by the City of Chicago for plumbing or electrical work, we handle all applications and coordination. We're experienced with Chicago's permitting process and building codes. Any permit costs are clearly outlined in your proposal. The permitting process typically takes 2-4 weeks when required.

How Do You Handle Condo Bathroom Remodeling And Building Requirements?

We specialize in downtown Chicago condo remodels and are highly experienced with building requirements. We prepare and submit all necessary documentation to your building or HOA, coordinate with building management for water shutoffs, respect elevator and noise restrictions, ensure proper waterproofing meets building standards, and comply with all building-specific rules. We've worked in hundreds of Chicago buildings and understand the unique requirements of high-rise living.

What's Your Payment Schedule For Bathroom Remodeling?

Our standard payment schedule is: (1) Deposit upon contract signing (typically 30-50%), (2) Payments at project milestones (demolition complete, rough-in complete, tile complete), (3) Final payment upon completion and your satisfaction. We never ask for full payment upfront, and we don't request final payment until you're completely satisfied with the work.

Can You Convert My Tub To A Walk-In Shower?

Yes, tub-to-shower conversions are one of our most popular bathroom remodeling services. This involves removing the existing tub, potentially raising the floor to accommodate new plumbing, installing a custom tile shower base, building and tiling shower walls, and adding glass enclosure or shower door. The result is a more spacious, modern, and accessible bathroom that better suits how most people actually use their bathrooms today.

Small Space Maximization: Making Every Square Foot Count

Chicago condos, especially in older buildings, often have limited square footage where every inch matters. Galley kitchens that feel like hallways. Bathrooms with awkward layouts. Wasted space around columns or mechanical systems. Generic builder layouts that don't optimize the footprint. Condo remodeling Chicago succeeds when it makes compact spaces feel significantly larger and function dramatically better.

The Wood Contracting team specializes in space-maximizing condo renovation. We reconfigure layouts to improve flow and usability, design custom storage that reaches ceilings and uses corners, select appropriately scaled fixtures and appliances, create visual tricks that expand perceived space, and eliminate the wasted areas that plague typical condo layouts.

Transform your compact condo from cramped and cluttered to open and organized through thoughtful design that respects the realities of downtown living.

Building And HOA Navigation: We Know The Process

The most frustrating part of condo remodeling Chicago is often the approval process. Every building has different requirements, forms, restrictions, and personalities managing the process. Some are straightforward, others are bureaucratic nightmares. First-time condo renovators get overwhelmed by insurance certificates, elevator scheduling, work hour restrictions, and endless documentation.

What we do differently: We've worked in hundreds of Chicago buildings and know what each requires. We prepare complete documentation packages upfront. We understand building engineer and management expectations. We schedule properly around building restrictions. We maintain professional relationships with building staff. We handle the bureaucracy so you don't have to become an expert in your building's remodeling rules.

We complete condo renovation Chicago projects smoothly because we've navigated these processes dozens of times before in buildings just like yours.

‍
High-Rise Logistics: Working 30 Floors Up

Condo remodeling in downtown Chicago high-rises presents unique logistical challenges that single-family contractors aren't equipped to handle. You can't just back a truck up to the door. Materials must go through loading docks, service elevators, and hallways. Debris removal requires coordination. Deliveries need scheduling days in advance. One missed elevator reservation can delay the entire project.

Wood Contracting's Chicago condo remodeling team excels at high-rise construction logistics. We schedule elevator reservations well ahead, coordinate deliveries with building loading docks, protect common areas during material transport, remove debris promptly and professionally, work within building-specific restrictions, and manage the complexity of construction 30 floors up without the chaos that unprepared contractors create.

Our condo renovation expertise shows in smooth project execution that respects your building, your neighbors, and the realities of working in occupied Chicago high-rises where everything is more complicated than ground-level construction.

Soundproofing And Neighbor Consideration

Living with shared walls means your condo remodeling Chicago impacts neighbors whether you like it or not. Construction noise travels through floors and walls. Early morning demolition wakes people up. Dust can migrate into adjacent units through ventilation. Inconsiderate contractors create building-wide frustration and complaints to management that can shut down your project.

We approach condo renovation with neighbor consideration built into our process: respecting strict work hour restrictions without exception, containing dust within your unit effectively, minimizing noise during demolition and installation, cleaning common areas if any debris escapes, maintaining professional demeanor with neighbors and staff, and adding soundproofing in shared walls when appropriate for long-term benefit.

What makes this work: Experience working in occupied buildings where neighbors matter. Understanding that your relationship with your building outlasts the renovation. Proper training on dust containment and protection. Professional crews who respect that this isn't a job site in the middle of nowhere. Our reputation depends on being good neighbors during your condo remodeling.

Condo remodeling Chicago requires navigating building requirements, HOA approvals, and tight spaces that demand creative solutions. Our condo renovation process handles everything from elevator coordination to soundproofing, transforming downtown Chicago condos while respecting your building's rules and your neighbors.

Consultation & Building Review

We begin your condo remodeling Chicago project by visiting your unit to assess the space and limitations, reviewing your condo association's remodeling requirements, discussing design goals and how you use your space, evaluating structural and system constraints, and establishing timelines that work with building work hour restrictions.

Design & Space Optimization

Our condo renovation Chicago team creates designs that maximize your limited square footage, work within building structural limitations, incorporate sound dampening for shared walls, plan efficient storage solutions, and select finishes appropriate for high-rise living. We design condos that feel significantly larger and function beautifully.

HOA Approvals & Documentation

Condo remodeling Chicago requires extensive documentation. We prepare and submit all required forms to your HOA or building management, obtain necessary approvals before work begins, coordinate elevator reservations and move-in/move-out fees, ensure compliance with building-specific rules, and handle all permit applications with the city.

Site Prep & Demo

Our team manages condo demolition with minimal disruption by protecting common areas and hallways during material transport, respecting noise restrictions and approved work hours, containing dust within your unit, removing all debris promptly, and maintaining professional relationships with building management and neighbors throughout your condo remodeling.

Precise Installation

During condo renovation, we install within tight tolerances required for high-rise construction, address soundproofing between units, work efficiently to minimize construction timeline, coordinate deliveries around building schedules, and ensure all work meets both building requirements and our quality standards for your downtown Chicago condo.

Final Inspection & Closeout

We complete your condo remodeling Chicago project with final inspections by city and building, thorough cleaning of your unit and common areas, documentation submission to building management, a detailed walkthrough with you, and confirmation that you're thrilled with your transformed condo and ready to enjoy your upgraded downtown Chicago living space.

What Makes Wood Contracting Condo Remodeling Different?

Structural Limitations And Creative Solutions

Condo remodeling Chicago works within fixed structural constraints you can't change. Load-bearing columns in inconvenient locations. Plumbing stacks that can't be moved. HVAC systems with limited capacity. Building structure that dictates what's possible with layout changes.

We evaluate structural realities during initial consultation, design around limitations creatively rather than fighting them, know when structural engineers are needed, and create solutions that make the best of your condo's actual construction rather than pretending constraints don't exist.

Condo-Appropriate Material Selections

Not all materials work well in condo environments. Heavy tile that exceeds floor load limits. Ventilation requirements for gas ranges in buildings with restrictions. Waterproofing standards that vary by building age. Appliances that don't fit through freight elevators or unit doors.

We select materials appropriate for high-rise living: lighter tile options for floor load compliance, proper waterproofing that protects units below, appliances sized for elevator and door clearances, and finishes that meet building requirements while delivering the look you want.

Coordination With Building Systems

Condo renovation requires coordination with building systems and staff that single-family work doesn't involve.

Critical coordination we handle: Scheduling water shutoffs with building engineers. Coordinating HVAC work with building systems. Working around building maintenance schedules. Ensuring electrical work doesn't impact other units. Managing waste removal through building protocols. Communicating with building management throughout. Coordinating final inspections with building and city. These details separate successful condo remodeling from projects that create building-wide problems.

Understanding Chicago Condo Buildings

We've completed condo remodeling in River North luxury towers, Gold Coast vintage conversions, South Loop loft buildings, Streeterville mid-rises. Each building type and era has different construction, rules, and renovation considerations.

You're not getting a contractor learning condo renovation on your project. You're getting a team with extensive experience in Chicago high-rise buildings who understand what works where.

Every condo remodeling Chicago project is unique, and your investment reflects your unit size, the scope of work, and the finishes you select. Condo remodels have some added complexity from building coordination and logistics, but deliver tremendous impact in transforming compact downtown spaces. Final pricing depends on extent of updates and finish quality.

Frequently Asked Questions About Condo Remodeling In Chicago

See the commonly asked questions Chicago homeowners ask when exploring condo remodeling.

How Long Does Condo Remodeling Take?

Most condo remodeling Chicago projects take 4-8 weeks from start to finish. Kitchen remodels typically take 4-6 weeks, bathroom remodels 3-5 weeks, and whole unit remodels 6-8 weeks. The timeline depends on scope of work, material lead times, building restrictions on work hours, and approval processes. We provide detailed timelines accounting for building-specific requirements in your proposal.

What Approvals Do I Need From My Building?

Condo remodeling Chicago requires extensive building coordination. You'll need approval from your HOA or building management for the scope of work, certificate of insurance naming the building, elevator reservation and move-in/move-out fees paid, proof of proper permitting from the city, and compliance with building rules on work hours, noise, and common area protection. We handle preparing and submitting all required documentation.

How Much Does Condo Remodeling Cost In Chicago?

Condo remodeling Chicago costs typically range from $12,000 for single bathroom updates to $100,000+ for complete unit gut remodels with luxury finishes. The main cost factors are square footage being remodeled, kitchen and bathroom scope, flooring and finishes throughout, building logistics and restrictions, and quality of materials selected. A typical condo kitchen remodel Chicago costs $22,000-$50,000. Full unit remodels typically cost $50,000-$100,000. We provide transparent, detailed proposals.

Can I Stay In My Condo During Remodeling?

For single room remodels like one bathroom, staying is manageable. For kitchen remodels, you'll be without a functional kitchen for 4-6 weeks, which most condo owners find difficult. For whole unit condo remodeling Chicago projects, we strongly recommend moving out temporarily since you'll be without essential facilities and living in active construction. We can discuss phasing options to keep spaces functional if staying.

What Work Hour Restrictions Do Buildings Have?

Most Chicago condo buildings restrict construction to weekdays between 8am-5pm or 9am-6pm, with no weekend work allowed. Some buildings are stricter. We respect all building restrictions on work hours, coordinate our schedule accordingly, and plan projects accounting for these limitations. This is factored into timeline estimates we provide for condo remodeling Chicago.

Can You Do Open Concept In A Condo?

Many Chicago condos benefit from removing walls between kitchen and living areas. However, we must work within structural limitations since you cannot modify load-bearing columns or building structure in condos. We evaluate what's possible during initial consultation, work with structural engineers if needed, and ensure all changes comply with building requirements and city permits for your condo remodel.

Do I Need City Permits For Condo Remodeling?

Yes, condo remodeling Chicago requires city permits for plumbing, electrical, and any structural work. We handle all permit applications with the City of Chicago, coordinate required inspections, ensure compliance with building codes, and provide permit documentation to your building management. Your building will typically require proof of permits before approving your project.

How Do You Minimize Disruption To Neighbors?

We take condo remodeling disruption seriously by protecting common areas and hallways during material transport, respecting building noise restrictions and work hours, containing dust within your unit with barriers, removing debris promptly via service elevators, maintaining professional communication with building staff, and being considerate neighbors throughout your condo remodeling Chicago project.

What's Included In Building Coordination?

For every condo remodeling Chicago project, we handle preparing all required HOA/building forms and documentation, submitting insurance certificates, reserving elevators and coordinating delivery schedules, paying required move-in/move-out fees, coordinating with building engineers for shutoffs if needed, ensuring compliance with all building-specific rules, and maintaining positive relationships with building management throughout your remodel.

Will Condo Remodeling Increase My Unit Value?

Yes, quality condo remodeling significantly increases unit value in Chicago's competitive downtown market. Updated kitchens and bathrooms provide the strongest returns, especially when builder-grade finishes are prevalent in your building. Well-executed condo remodeling Chicago typically returns 70-90% of investment at resale while you enjoy a dramatically improved living space. In desirable buildings and neighborhoods, remodeled units command substantial premiums.

Dillon stays on site throughout and deals with building management directly instead of leaving it to a sub.

Most of our condo projects sit in and around downtown, including River North, Streeterville, Gold Coast, the South Loop, the West Loop, Printer's Row, and Old Town. We also remodel units further out in Lincoln Park, Lakeview, Wicker Park, Bucktown, Logan Square, Roscoe Village, Ravenswood, and Hyde Park.

You've been living with compromises long enough. The kitchen layout that never worked. Bathrooms stuck in the wrong decade. A basement gathering dust. Flooring that should have been replaced years ago. Whole home remodeling Chicago lets you fix everything at once, creating a completely transformed home that finally works for how you actually live. If you are still deciding, our remodel or move decision guide lays out the math.

Wood Contracting specializes in home remodeling Chicago, from Lincoln Park greystones to South Loop condos. We handle complete remodels that coordinate multiple spaces, manage complex timelines across trades, navigate Chicago building codes and permits, and deliver the quality you expect when investing this significantly in your home. A whole-home remodel in Chicago typically takes 8 to 16 weeks and ranges from about $50,000 to $200,000+, depending on scope and finishes. One licensed owner, Dillon Wood, coordinates everything with his dedicated crew.

Complete Home Transformation: Fixing Everything That's Wrong At Once

Living with a house that doesn't work creates daily frustration. The kitchen layout forces awkward workflow. Bathrooms are cramped or outdated. The basement sits unfinished. Flooring from three different decades. Lighting that's inadequate in every room. Whole home remodeling Chicago addresses everything systematically instead of piecemeal projects that never quite come together.

The Wood Contracting team specializes in comprehensive home renovation Chicago. We create unified design plans across all spaces, coordinate construction sequencing to minimize disruption, manage multiple trades efficiently, ensure consistent quality throughout your home, and transform houses that feel cobbled together into cohesive homes that finally work.

Transform your entire home in one coordinated project instead of living through years of ongoing construction and never quite getting the house you want.

Historic Chicago Home Renovation: Respecting Character While Modernizing Everything

Lincoln Park greystones, Bucktown vintage homes, and Old Town buildings have beautiful bones but systems and layouts from another era. Original plumbing and electrical that's decades past replacement. Layouts designed for different lifestyles. Beautiful millwork and details worth preserving mixed with desperate need for modern functionality. Home remodeling Chicago for historic properties requires balancing preservation with comprehensive updates.

What we do differently: Updating all mechanical systems to current code while hiding modern requirements. Preserving original millwork, hardwood, and architectural details. Reconfiguring layouts for contemporary living while respecting the home's character. Installing modern kitchens and bathrooms that feel appropriate to the era. Working with plaster walls and uneven floors common in older construction.

We transform vintage Chicago homes into comfortable, modern residences that honor their history while functioning perfectly for how families live today.

‍
Condo Whole Home Remodeling: Transforming Your Entire Unit

Downtown Chicago condos built 15-20 years ago feel tired throughout. Builder-grade everything in kitchen and baths. Generic flooring. Inadequate lighting. Layouts that waste space. Paint colors from 2005. Whole unit renovation makes sense when every room needs attention and you want a cohesive, modern result rather than a patchwork of updates over years.

Wood Contracting's home remodeling Chicago team excels at complete condo transformations. We handle all building and HOA approvals before work begins, coordinate elevator reservations and deliveries, work within strict noise and hour restrictions, design space-maximizing solutions for compact footprints, ensure soundproofing between units, and manage the unique challenges of high-rise construction logistics.

Our whole home condo renovations create sophisticated, cohesive units that feel completely custom rather than builder-grade. From River North to South Loop, we transform dated condos into spaces you're proud to call home and that command premium prices in Chicago's competitive market.

Open Concept Transformations: Reimagining How Your Home Flows

Many Chicago homes have choppy layouts with small, closed-off rooms that don't match how families actually live. Kitchens isolated from dining and living areas. Formal dining rooms rarely used. Compartmentalized spaces when you want openness and connection. Whole home remodeling is the opportunity to fundamentally reimagine your home's flow and how spaces relate.

We transform closed floor plans into open, connected homes by removing non-structural walls strategically, installing beams for structural support where needed, creating sightlines that connect spaces, designing cohesive flow from room to room, and maintaining appropriate separation where privacy matters.

What makes this work: Understanding which walls can be removed and structural requirements. Knowing Chicago building codes for open concept conversions. Experience with permit requirements for structural changes. Skill in creating open plans that still feel defined rather than one giant room. Design sense that makes the result feel intentional, not like walls were just removed.

Featured Home Transformation: Third-Floor Patio Conversion In Logan Square

The Challenge

This Logan Square home had a third-floor outdoor patio that seemed like a luxury when the homeowners bought the place, but reality set in quickly. Chicago weather meant the space sat unused eight months of the year. Snow piled up in winter. Spring and fall were too cold. Even summer had maybe 60 truly comfortable days. The patio represented nearly 250 square feet of potential living space going completely to waste while the third-floor unit felt cramped with no home office, inadequate storage, and a layout that didn't work for how the family actually lived. The challenge was converting outdoor space to conditioned interior square footage in an older building with structural considerations, weatherproofing requirements, and the reality that this needed to feel like original interior space, not an obvious add-on.

‍

Our Solution

We designed a complete patio conversion that transformed unused outdoor space into a bright, functional home office and storage room. Structural engineering confirmed the existing patio structure could support interior buildout with proper reinforcement. We fully enclosed the space with energy-efficient windows that maximize natural light while providing insulation, installed proper weatherproofing and moisture barriers critical for converted exterior spaces, extended HVAC from the main unit to ensure year-round comfort, and added electrical with dedicated circuits and ample outlets for office equipment. The new space features luxury vinyl flooring and finishes that match the existing third-floor space so the conversion feels seamless rather than tacked on. All work was coordinated with the homeowner and completed in compliance with Chicago building codes for converting exterior to interior space.

‍

The Result

The completed patio conversion added nearly 250 square feet of highly functional, climate-controlled living space to this Logan Square home. The homeowner now has an expanded space with abundant natural light, and the whole unit functions dramatically better with room to grow. Instead of an outdoor space used 60 days a year, the family gained an interior room they use 365 days a year. This whole home remodeling in Chicago demonstrates how creative space conversion can add serious square footage and value to Chicago multi-family buildings without the complexity and cost of ground-up additions.

Our Whole Home Remodeling Chicago Process

Whole home remodeling Chicago transforms your entire house from top to bottom, updating everything from kitchens and bathrooms to flooring, lighting, and layouts. Our comprehensive renovation process manages complex projects involving multiple trades, keeping everything coordinated and on schedule.

Whole Home Consultation

We begin your whole home remodeling Chicago project by walking through every room and space in your home, discussing your vision for each area and how spaces connect, identifying structural or system upgrades needed, reviewing your timeline and whether you'll stay during construction, and establishing overall project scope and investment for your complete home renovation.

Design & Planning

Our whole home renovation team creates detailed plans covering every space being remodeled, shows how rooms flow and connect throughout your home, specifies all materials and finishes for consistency, coordinates mechanical, electrical, and plumbing upgrades, and develops a construction sequence that makes sense for whole home remodeling Chicago projects.

Permitting & Project Staging

Whole home remodeling requires comprehensive permits and planning. We handle all permit applications for structural, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical work, create a phased construction schedule, coordinate material deliveries and storage, plan for living arrangements if you're staying in the home, and ensure your Chicago home renovation proceeds smoothly from start to finish.

Demo & Infrastructure

Our team approaches whole home renovation systematically by removing finishes and fixtures according to the project plan, updating electrical panels and wiring throughout, replacing or upgrading plumbing systems, addressing HVAC for whole home comfort, and ensuring infrastructure updates set the foundation for your transformed Chicago home.

Room-By-Room Renovation

During whole home remodeling Chicago, we execute renovations in a coordinated sequence, complete kitchen and bathroom installations, install new flooring throughout, update all lighting and electrical, add custom cabinetry and built-ins, and maintain quality and attention to detail in every single room of your renovated home.

Final Finishes & Home Reveal

We complete your whole home renovation Chicago with final paint throughout, hardware and fixture installation, thorough cleaning of every space, punch list completion, and an exciting final walkthrough where you experience your completely transformed home and begin this new chapter of living in a space that finally works perfectly for you.

What Makes Wood Contracting Chicago Whole Home Remodeling Different?
Learn More About Us
Project Management That Keeps Everything Coordinated

Whole home remodeling involves coordinating multiple trades across weeks or months. Electricians, plumbers, HVAC, tile installers, painters, flooring specialists, and more must work in proper sequence. One delay cascades through everything.

We manage the entire project timeline, coordinate all subcontractors and deliveries, ensure work happens in logical sequence, solve problems before they cause delays, and keep you informed without overwhelming you with construction minutiae.

Cohesive Design Across Every Space

The difference between a whole home renovation and random room updates is cohesion. Flooring that flows logically. Consistent trim and door styles. Coordinated color palettes. Lighting that creates unified ambiance. Hardware and fixture finishes that relate.

We help you make selections that create visual flow throughout your home rather than rooms that feel disconnected or styles that clash when you walk from space to space.

Systems Updates: The Unglamorous Essentials

Whole home remodeling is the time to address systems you can't see but desperately need: outdated electrical panels and wiring, old plumbing that should be replaced, inadequate HVAC capacity, poor insulation, and structural issues.

Critical updates we handle: Electrical panel upgrades and rewiring throughout. Replacing old plumbing before it fails. HVAC system sizing and efficiency improvements. Insulation upgrades for comfort and energy savings. Structural repairs or reinforcement. Foundation or moisture issues. These aren't sexy but they're essential for homes that work properly.

Understanding Chicago Home Renovation Complexity

We've completed whole home renovations in Lincoln Park 100-year-old greystones, South Loop modern condos, Wicker Park vintage two-flats, Bucktown single-families. Every building era and type presents different challenges for comprehensive renovation.

You're not getting a contractor learning whole home remodeling on your project. You're getting a team with extensive experience managing complex, multi-space Chicago renovations from start to finish.

Every home remodeling Chicago project is unique, and your investment reflects the size of your home, the scope of work, and the finishes you select. Remodeling multiple spaces provides economies of scale compared to tackling rooms individually over time. Final pricing depends on structural changes, systems updates, and finish quality throughout. Frequently Asked Questions About Whole Home Remodeling In Chicago

See the commonly asked questions Chicago homeowners ask when exploring complete home remodel.

How Long Does Whole Home Remodeling Take?

Most complete home remodeling Chicago projects take 8-16 weeks from start to finish. The timeline depends on the scope of work, number of rooms being remodeled, whether you're doing structural changes, permitting and inspection schedules, and material lead times. A typical whole home remodel touching kitchen, bathrooms, and finishes takes 10-14 weeks. We provide a detailed timeline with your proposal showing the construction sequence.

Can I Stay In My Home During Remodel?

It depends on the scope of your home remodeling Chicago project. For remodels affecting kitchen and multiple bathrooms simultaneously, most families choose to move out temporarily since you'll be without essential facilities for weeks. For phased remodels where we complete spaces sequentially, staying is more manageable but still disruptive. We can structure the work to keep at least one bathroom functional if you're staying. We'll discuss living arrangements honestly during planning.

How Much Does Whole Home Remodeling Cost In Chicago?

Home remodeling Chicago costs typically range from $50,000 for focused multi-room updates to $200,000+ for complete gut remodels with high-end finishes. The main cost factors are square footage of your home, number of rooms being remodeled, kitchen and bathroom scope, structural or layout changes, finish quality selections, and mechanical system updates. A typical whole home remodeling project in Chicago costs $50,000-$100,000. We provide detailed, transparent proposals breaking down costs by space and category.

Do You Provide Design Services For Whole Home Remodel?

We partner with two exceptional local interior designers experienced in comprehensive Chicago home remodels. For whole home remodeling, professional design services are highly recommended to ensure cohesive flow between spaces, consistent material selections throughout, proper space planning, and a unified vision. You can work with our partner designers, your own designer, or we can help coordinate selections without formal design services.

What's Involved In Planning A Whole Home Remodel?

Planning home remodeling Chicago requires comprehensive coordination. We start with assessing every space being remodeled, discussing your vision and priorities, creating detailed scope of work, developing construction sequencing, coordinating all material selections and lead times, planning for living arrangements during construction, and establishing realistic budgets and timelines. Good planning is critical for whole home projects to avoid delays and budget overruns.

Should I Remodel Everything At Once Or In Phases?

Remodeling everything at once is typically more cost-effective and less disruptive long-term than phasing over years. Benefits include one mobilization and setup, coordinated material orders, consistent finishes throughout, single permit process, and getting it done rather than living in construction intermittently. However, budget constraints sometimes necessitate phasing. We can help you decide the best approach for your home remodeling Chicago project.

Do You Handle Permits For Whole Home Remodeling?

Yes, comprehensive home remodeling Chicago requires extensive permitting for structural, electrical, plumbing, mechanical work, and changes to living spaces. We handle all permit applications with the City of Chicago, coordinate required inspections throughout construction, ensure all work meets building codes, and manage the permitting timeline so it doesn't delay your project. Permit costs are clearly outlined in your proposal.

Can Whole Home Remodeling Include Layout Changes?

Absolutely. Whole home remodel is the ideal time for layout improvements: removing walls to open spaces, reconfiguring kitchens for better workflow, adding bathrooms or converting bedroom layouts, finishing basements into living spaces, and reimagining how rooms connect and flow. We work with structural engineers when needed for load-bearing walls and ensure all changes meet Chicago building codes.

What's Your Payment Schedule For Whole Home Projects?

Our standard payment schedule for home remodeling Chicago is: (1) Initial deposit upon contract signing (typically 20-30%), (2) Progress payments tied to completion milestones (demolition, rough-in, substantial completion of each major space), (3) Final payment upon project completion and your satisfaction. For large projects, payments are typically divided across 4-6 milestones. We never ask for full payment upfront.

Will Whole Home Remodeling Increase My Home Value?

Yes, comprehensive home remodeling Chicago typically provides strong return on investment, especially in desirable Chicago neighborhoods. Updated kitchens and bathrooms add the most value, but whole home consistency and modern systems are increasingly important to buyers. Most homeowners see 65-85% return on investment at resale, while immediately enjoying a completely transformed home. For families planning to stay long-term, the value is living in the home you want without moving.

Frequently Asked Questions About Basement Finishing In Chicago

See the commonly asked questions Chicago homeowners ask when exploring basement finishing.

How Long Does Basement Finishing Take?

Most complete basement finishing projects take 4-8 weeks from start to completion. Smaller spaces like a single room or home office can be completed in 4-5 weeks, while full basement buildouts with multiple rooms, bathrooms, and wet bars take 6-8 weeks. The timeline depends on square footage, complexity of layout, whether we're adding plumbing, egress window installation, and addressing any moisture or foundation issues. We provide a detailed timeline in your proposal.

Can You Finish A Basement With Low Ceilings?

Yes, many Chicago basements have ceiling heights between 7 and 8 feet, which is workable for finished living space. We use strategies to maximize headroom: flush mount lighting instead of fixtures that hang down, spray foam insulation that's thinner than traditional batts, efficient HVAC solutions, and careful planning around ductwork and pipes. If your basement is under 7 feet, we evaluate whether finishing makes sense or if other solutions work better.

How Much Does Basement Finishing Cost In Chicago?

Basement remodeling costs in Chicago typically range from $10,000 for basic single room conversions to $80,000+ for complete luxury buildouts with multiple rooms, bathrooms, and high-end finishes. The main cost factors are square footage being finished, framing and drywall, flooring throughout, electrical and lighting, HVAC extensions, egress windows if required, bathroom additions, and finish quality. A typical mid-range basement remodel Chicago costs $25,000-$50,000. We provide detailed, transparent proposals so you understand exactly where your investment goes.

Do You Provide Basement Design Services?

We partner with two exceptional local interior designers who specialize in basement layouts and space planning. Both have extensive experience designing Chicago basements for every purpose and budget. Alternatively, you can work with your own designer, or we can help you plan the layout and select finishes without formal design services. We're flexible to match your needs and preferences.

What Moisture Issues Should I Address Before Finishing?

Before finishing any Chicago basement, we evaluate moisture conditions carefully. Common issues include foundation seepage, condensation on walls, poor drainage around the foundation, sump pump failures, and high humidity. We address moisture at the source through proper waterproofing, installing or upgrading sump pumps, improving exterior drainage, applying moisture barriers to walls, and specifying moisture-resistant materials. Finishing over existing moisture problems always fails, so we handle this right from the start.

Do I Need Egress Windows In My Finished Basement?

Chicago building code requires egress windows in basement bedrooms for safety. If you're creating a bedroom or guest suite, we'll need to install at least one egress window that meets size requirements for emergency escape. For rec rooms, home offices, or other non-sleeping spaces, egress windows aren't legally required but are often worth adding for natural light and resale value. We handle all egress window installation, cutting, waterproofing, and well installation.

Do You Handle Permits For Basement Finishing?

Yes, basement remodeling Chicago IL requires building permits for the work we do: framing, electrical, plumbing, egress windows, and converting unfinished space to living space. We handle all permit applications and inspections. We're experienced with Chicago's permitting process and building codes for basements. Permit costs are clearly outlined in your proposal. The permitting process typically takes 2-4 weeks.

Can You Add A Bathroom In My Basement?

Yes, adding a basement bathroom is one of our most common requests, especially for guest suites or in-law spaces. This requires plumbing installation which can be straightforward or complex depending on your existing plumbing configuration. In homes with basement bathrooms roughed in, it's relatively simple. Otherwise, we may need to install an ejector pump to move waste up to your main sewer line. We evaluate your specific situation and provide clear pricing for bathroom additions.

What's Your Payment Schedule For Basement Finishing?

Our standard payment schedule is: (1) Deposit upon contract signing (typically 30-50%), (2) Payments at project milestones (framing complete, drywall complete, finishes complete), (3) Final payment upon completion and your satisfaction. We never ask for full payment upfront, and we don't request final payment until you're completely satisfied with the work.

Will Finishing My Basement Add Value To My Home?

Yes, finishing your basement typically provides strong return on investment for Chicago homes. A professionally finished basement adds livable square footage, which directly increases home value. The exact return depends on your neighborhood, quality of finishes, and what you create (bathrooms and additional bedrooms add more value than basic rec rooms). Most homeowners see 60-75% return on investment, while also enjoying the space themselves. For families needing more room without moving, the value is even higher.

What's The Difference Between Custom Cabinets And Semi-Custom?

Custom cabinets are built to your exact specifications for your specific space. Every dimension, every shelf height, every finish detail is designed for you. Semi custom cabinets start with standard sizes that can be modified slightly. Custom Chicago cabinets eliminate wasted space, fit perfectly in challenging layouts, accommodate your exact storage needs, and can match architectural details. For Chicago homes with unique dimensions or historic features, custom is often the only option that truly works.

Custom cabinets Chicago pricing typically ranges from $2,000 for small bathroom vanities to $20,000+ for complete kitchen cabinet installations with premium materials. A typical custom kitchen cabinet project in Chicago costs $15,000-$25,000. Custom built-ins for entertainment centers or home offices typically cost $3,000-$10,000. Do You Provide Design Services For Custom Cabinetry?

Yes, design consultation is included with every custom cabinetry project. We measure your space precisely, discuss how you'll use the storage, review material and finish options, create detailed plans showing dimensions and layout, and refine the design until it's exactly what you need. Our goal is cabinetry that looks great and functions perfectly for how you actually live.

Can You Match Existing Cabinetry Or Woodwork?

Yes, we regularly match existing cabinets, trim, or architectural details in Chicago homes. This is especially important in historic homes or when adding cabinets to kitchens in phases. We can match wood species, stain colors, door styles, and finish details. We bring samples to ensure accurate matching before fabrication begins.

What Types Of Wood Do You Use For Custom Cabinets?

We work with a full range of cabinet-grade woods including maple, cherry, oak, walnut, and hickory for traditional options, and painted finishes on maple or MDF for contemporary looks. Each wood has different characteristics for grain, color, and durability. We help you select the best material for your design style, budget, and how the cabinets will be used.

Can You Create Built-Ins For Odd-Shaped Spaces?

Absolutely. Custom built-ins excel in challenging spaces: alcoves with unusual dimensions, rooms with angled walls, spaces around windows or architectural features, areas with low ceilings or soffits, and layouts where standard furniture simply won't fit. We measure precisely and design solutions that make awkward spaces feel intentional and functional.

Yes, quality custom cabinetry typically provides strong return on investment, especially in Chicago's competitive real estate market. Custom kitchen cabinets are particularly valuable, often returning 60-80% of investment at resale while you enjoy them daily. Built-in storage solutions also appeal to buyers because they maximize usable space in ways that furniture cannot.

What's Your Payment Schedule For Custom Cabinetry?

We never ask for full payment upfront, and we don't request final payment until you're completely satisfied.

Old Town homeowners come to Wood Contracting for kitchen, bathroom, and whole-home remodeling led by a contractor with more than 30 years of hands-on experience. We remodel kitchens, bathrooms, and whole homes across the frame cottages and Victorian row houses of the Old Town Triangle landmark district, the vintage walk-ups, and the Wells Street condos. Bathrooms typically take 4 to 6 weeks and kitchens 6 to 10, with cost ranges in the summary below. We hold Illinois GC license TGC105501, are EPA Lead-Safe certified, carry full insurance, and coordinate city permits, landmark review where it applies, and any association approvals your building requires.

‍

Old Town Remodeling At A Glance

Here is what most Old Town homeowners want to know up front:

Kitchen remodels: $15,000 to $80,000+, depending on finishes and how much the layout or original infrastructure changes.
Bathroom remodels: $12,000 to $55,000+, from a powder room update to a full primary bathroom.
Timelines: expect 4 to 6 weeks for a bathroom, 6 to 10 for a kitchen, and 10 to 16 for a whole home.
Approvals: homes in the Old Town Triangle landmark district can add a review of exterior changes; a condo or walk-up may add an association sign-off; most interior work still needs a city permit. We coordinate whichever applies.
Older-home realities: these are some of the oldest homes in the city, so balloon framing, knob-and-tube wiring, and out-of-square floors are common. We account for them before the first wall comes down.
Credentials: Illinois GC license TGC105501, EPA Lead-Safe certified, fully insured.
Starting out: a free consultation with Dillon, usually arranged within the same week.

‍

Why Old Town Homeowners Trust Wood Contracting

Old Town pairs some of the oldest surviving homes in Chicago, frame cottages and Victorian row houses, many inside the Old Town Triangle landmark district, with vintage walk-ups and newer Wells Street condos. The contractor you choose has to respect that history and modernize at the same time, and on a landmarked block that means knowing what review the work will trigger before you start. Respecting the history while modernizing the home is our specialty, and about 90% of our work comes from referrals and repeat clients who have seen us do it.

Every consultation begins with Dillon Wood in person rather than a salesperson, so the person responsible for the result is there from the outset.

We have earned that the slow way, one old house at a time. We have remodeled Old Town's frame cottages, Victorian row houses, vintage walk-ups, and Wells Street condos, including kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, and full historic-home renovations. We know what hides behind the plaster in a 150-year-old cottage and how to modernize it without erasing the character that makes Old Town what it is.

Kitchen Remodeling In Old Town

Old Town holds some of the oldest homes in the city, built with tiny rear kitchens and additions stacked on over a century, so the work usually opens the space without losing a load-bearing wall or a stack that cannot move. The structure decides the plan before any finish does.

Our kitchen remodeling then installs cabinetry, quartz or natural stone counters, tile or stone backsplash, and appliances, either matching period detail or going fully modern inside the historic shell.

Bathroom Remodeling In Old Town

Open a wall in an Old Town bathroom and the age shows: balloon framing, cast-iron drains, galvanized lines, and plaster over a century of movement. We open it and rebuild on a sound base instead of patching over it.

With rooms below, waterproofing comes first, and our bathroom remodeling sets pan and membrane correctly before adding curbless showers, soaking tubs, double vanities, and heated floors.

Whole-Home, Row House, And Condo Renovations

A full historic-home renovation is some of our most rewarding Old Town work: kitchen, every bathroom, flooring, and layout updated while period detail and, on landmarked blocks, the exterior are protected. Most take 10 to 16 weeks.

That whole home renovation depends heavily on custom carpentry and built-ins to match original millwork, and many homes finish a lower level with basement finishing. Walk-ups and newer buildings get full condo renovation.

What Renovating An Old Town Home Actually Looks Like

What a project needs hinges on the property. A home in the Old Town Triangle landmark district can add exterior review on top of the city permit, a condo or walk-up can add an association sign-off, and an interior remodel of an unlandmarked home is mostly a permit matter. We pin that down before demolition and prepare the paperwork.

Work touching plumbing, electrical, or structure requires a Chicago permit. We advise when one applies and coordinate it with any landmark or association review, generally a 2 to 4 week city window.

What To Expect During Your Remodeling Journey

Our remodeling process is all about simplicity, transparency, and setting proper expectations. Remodeling projects can be stressful and we're here to make it as easy as possible.

1. Free Estimate

We'll do a site visit to see your space, take measurements, and walk you through your options with a free, no-commitment estimate.

2. Proposal

You'll get a clear, itemized proposal that breaks down the full scope of work, timeline, and costs to get a straightforward look at exactly what you're getting.

3. Design Selection

Work with our team or your designer to select materials, finishes, and fixtures. We'll handle permits, your HOA, and any building coordination.

4. Build

Our dedicated team completes your project with careful attention to detail. Dillon or your project manager communicates throughout and ensures quality at every stage.

5. Final Review

We review every detail together and address any items immediately. Your project is backed by our 1-year workmanship warranty.

A kitchen remodel typically takes 6 to 10 weeks from demo to completion. Bathroom remodels usually require 4 to 6 weeks. Whole home renovations generally need 10 to 16 weeks. Timeline depends on project scope and any required approvals.

Yes, Chicago building permits are required for most kitchen and bathroom remodels that involve plumbing, electrical, or structural changes. We advise you on when a permit is needed and coordinate permit pull-through when the project scope calls for it. Permits typically take 2 to 4 weeks.

What's The Best Time To Start A Renovation?

We work year-round in Chicago, though late fall through early spring can sometimes offer more flexible scheduling. The best time to start is when you're ready and have a clear vision for your project.

Bathroom remodels range from $12,000 for powder room updates to $55,000+ for luxury primary bathrooms. Half baths typically cost $12,000 to $20,000, full bathrooms run $20,000 to $32,000+, and primary bathrooms with custom features cost $32,000 to $55,000+.

Old Town properties have unique characteristics that influence renovation planning. We're familiar with historic district preservation, Victorian architecture, cobblestone streets, established neighborhood and can guide you through the process specific to this neighborhood.
