Kitchen and bathroom remodels typically offer strong returns in Old Town's competitive real estate market, often recouping 65% to 85% of the investment. Beyond resale value, the improved functionality provides immediate quality of life benefits.

Get in touch by phone, email, or the contact form to book your free consultation. We usually respond within one business day and can often come by the same week.

Two stages of remodeling over two years, and now it feels like home. 🤍

Foundry main floor remodel, Lakeville, MN.

#WhiteBirchDesign #LakevilleMN #MainFloorRemodel #KitchenRemodel #MinnesotaHomes

How long does a kitchen remodel actually take? 🏡

For a full remodel, plan on 5 to 7 months from the first conversation to the final walkthrough. 

About half of that time happens before demo day, and that planning is what keeps construction on track.

Swipe through the five phases to see what each one involves and how long it takes. 👉

Thinking about a kitchen project in 2027? Now is the perfect time to start the design conversation. Planning something smaller? We still have a few openings left this year.

📌 Save this for when you’re ready to plan, and reach out through the link in bio. No start date or final design needed, just a conversation.

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #RemodelingTips #designbuildmn 

5 to 7 months covers a full remodel from first conversation to final walkthrough. A cosmetic refresh (new countertops, hardware, paint, and lighting) can move faster. Removing walls or relocating plumbing and electrical puts you toward the longer end.

We start with an initial consultation about your goals, priorities, and general budget range, then a site visit to assess your space and any structural constraints. Early renderings show you what’s possible before anything is decided. This is also where your overall timeline comes into focus.

Showroom visits are one of our favorite parts. Seeing materials in person, side by side and in different light, makes all the difference. Quick deciders move faster, and if you’re still exploring, that’s completely fine. Better to land it here than change course after cabinets are ordered.

Once your contract is signed, we start ordering your selections, many from local Minnesota vendors. Behind the scenes, we’re:
- Placing orders for every selection
- Finalizing permits, if required
- Confirming delivery windows

Many homes built in the ‘90s have closed-off kitchens, half walls, and separate dining rooms, so opening them up often takes structural work. Once walls open, we sometimes find outdated electrical or off-code plumbing. We plan for those surprises and tell you right away when one comes up. Tip: most homeowners set up a temporary kitchen in another room.

The punch list is a detailed walkthrough of everyth

Designed for a family that gathers often, with a main floor that has a place for everyone. 

The character comes from the details. 

Here are nine from this Lakeville main floor remodel: 
1. A stone fireplace up to the existing soffit, under 18-foot ceilings 
2. White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain, with champagne bronze hardware 
3. A custom iron railing from a local ironworker 
4. Tambour on the dining room walls, with sconces 
5. A Tambour wall in the piano room 
6. Tambour on the back of the island, with a Zellige tile backsplash 
7. A custom arched hutch 
8. A powder room gone dark, with wood-textured tile 
9. A cabinet that hides the printer 

Save this one for your own main floor, and see the full project at the link in bio under Kitchen.

#MainFloorRemodel #twincitiesremodeler #LakevilleMN #mndesignbuild #whitebirchdesign 

Start here: a stone fireplace that climbs to the existing soffit under 18-foot ceilings, right at the center of the floor.

White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain and champagne bronze hardware bring warmth to all that stone.

The stairs got a custom iron railing from a local ironworker, and the carpet carries right up beside it.

Take out the soffits and columns, and the dining room opens right up. A Tambour detail brings the texture.

Right across from the dining room, the piano room picks up the same Tambour detail, with sconces on the wall.

Look closely. The Tambour detail follows you into the kitchen on the back of the island, and a Zellige tile backsplash adds more texture.

The custom arched hutch gives this kitchen even more personality.

Then a surprise: the powder room goes dark, with wood-textured tile.

Even the office got a plan: a custom white oak desk and a cabinet that hides the printer. 

Which room is your favorite?

We’re not saying a new kitchen fixes everything. 👀 

We’re just saying nobody has ever been sad about warm white oak cabinets and a custom hood. 🙌 

Fun fact: that hood was finished by a local artisan in a custom color and texture, and it gives the whole room its character. 

First peek at our Foundry Kitchen remodel. Ready to start yours? DM us and let’s talk. 

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #SouthMetroMN #MNDesignBuild

Behind every finished kitchen photo is a lot of nudging, fussing, and “wait, one more inch to the left.” 😄 

Swipe through our latest photo shoot to see what goes into capturing a space the way it deserves: 

🕯️ Finding the perfect placement 
🍏 A little pop of green before the shutter clicks 
📷 Getting every angle just right 
👯 A crew that makes it fun 

The details you live with every day, like the cabinetry, the lighting, and the way a room flows, deserve to be seen properly. That’s why we take the photos as seriously as the build. 

The final reveal is coming soon. 

Thinking about a kitchen, bath, or basement remodel? DM us or tap the link in our bio and let’s talk. 

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #mndesignbuild #twincitiesremodeler

What a whirlwind weekend at R20! Thank you to everyone who stopped by the Parade of Homes Remodelers Showcase. We loved meeting you, hearing about your projects, and answering your questions.

A choppy layout and a few partial walls were boxing in this Lakeville, MN kitchen. Once they came down, it got the room it was always meant to have:

🤍 An island scaled for real life
🤍 A built-in beverage center made for hosting
🤍 Hickory floors running through the whole main level, so it all reads as one space

Missed us, or living with a layout that feels chopped up? Tell us what’s not working. Link in bio to get started.

Foundry main floor remodel, Lakeville, MN.

How long does a kitchen remodel actually take? 🏡

For a full remodel, plan on 5 to 7 months from the first conversation to the final walkthrough. 

About half of that time happens before demo day, and that planning is what keeps construction on track.

Swipe through the five phases to see what each one involves and how long it takes. 👉

Thinking about a kitchen project in 2027? Now is the perfect time to start the design conversation. Planning something smaller? We still have a few openings left this year.

📌 Save this for when you’re ready to plan, and reach out through the link in bio. No start date or final design needed, just a conversation.

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #RemodelingTips #designbuildmn 

5 to 7 months covers a full remodel from first conversation to final walkthrough. A cosmetic refresh (new countertops, hardware, paint, and lighting) can move faster. Removing walls or relocating plumbing and electrical puts you toward the longer end.

We start with an initial consultation about your goals, priorities, and general budget range, then a site visit to assess your space and any structural constraints. Early renderings show you what’s possible before anything is decided. This is also where your overall timeline comes into focus.

Showroom visits are one of our favorite parts. Seeing materials in person, side by side and in different light, makes all the difference. Quick deciders move faster, and if you’re still exploring, that’s completely fine. Better to land it here than change course after cabinets are ordered.

Once your contract is signed, we start ordering your selections, many from local Minnesota vendors. Behind the scenes, we’re:
- Placing orders for every selection
- Finalizing permits, if required
- Confirming delivery windows

Many homes built in the ‘90s have closed-off kitchens, half walls, and separate dining rooms, so opening them up often takes structural work. Once walls open, we sometimes find outdated electrical or off-code plumbing. We plan for those surprises and tell you right away when one comes up. Tip: most homeowners set up a temporary kitchen in another room.

The punch list is a detailed walkthrough of everyth

Designed for a family that gathers often, with a main floor that has a place for everyone. 

The character comes from the details. 

Here are nine from this Lakeville main floor remodel: 
1. A stone fireplace up to the existing soffit, under 18-foot ceilings 
2. White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain, with champagne bronze hardware 
3. A custom iron railing from a local ironworker 
4. Tambour on the dining room walls, with sconces 
5. A Tambour wall in the piano room 
6. Tambour on the back of the island, with a Zellige tile backsplash 
7. A custom arched hutch 
8. A powder room gone dark, with wood-textured tile 
9. A cabinet that hides the printer 

Save this one for your own main floor, and see the full project at the link in bio under Kitchen.

#MainFloorRemodel #twincitiesremodeler #LakevilleMN #mndesignbuild #whitebirchdesign 

Start here: a stone fireplace that climbs to the existing soffit under 18-foot ceilings, right at the center of the floor.

White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain and champagne bronze hardware bring warmth to all that stone.

The stairs got a custom iron railing from a local ironworker, and the carpet carries right up beside it.

Take out the soffits and columns, and the dining room opens right up. A Tambour detail brings the texture.

Right across from the dining room, the piano room picks up the same Tambour detail, with sconces on the wall.

Look closely. The Tambour detail follows you into the kitchen on the back of the island, and a Zellige tile backsplash adds more texture.

The custom arched hutch gives this kitchen even more personality.

Then a surprise: the powder room goes dark, with wood-textured tile.

Even the office got a plan: a custom white oak desk and a cabinet that hides the printer. 

Which room is your favorite?

We’re not saying a new kitchen fixes everything. 👀 

We’re just saying nobody has ever been sad about warm white oak cabinets and a custom hood. 🙌 

Fun fact: that hood was finished by a local artisan in a custom color and texture, and it gives the whole room its character. 

First peek at our Foundry Kitchen remodel. Ready to start yours? DM us and let’s talk. 

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #SouthMetroMN #MNDesignBuild

Behind every finished kitchen photo is a lot of nudging, fussing, and “wait, one more inch to the left.” 😄 

Swipe through our latest photo shoot to see what goes into capturing a space the way it deserves: 

🕯️ Finding the perfect placement 
🍏 A little pop of green before the shutter clicks 
📷 Getting every angle just right 
👯 A crew that makes it fun 

The details you live with every day, like the cabinetry, the lighting, and the way a room flows, deserve to be seen properly. That’s why we take the photos as seriously as the build. 

The final reveal is coming soon.

Our Values

Here at White Birch Design, we pride ourselves on offering many of the ‘perks’ of the larger design/build companies (experienced design and project management) without the big price tag and impersonal communication.

Our boutique like approach to kitchen, bath and basement remodeling is affordable and specialized. We offer high-quality work and excellent customer service with a personal approach, inviting homeowners to feel a part of the process and valued as a customer.

Our company was founded on principles which we are committed to upholding in every home transformation we undertake.

INTEGRITY

Accountable, trustworthy, honest, fair, and respectful

QUALITY

Quality materials and quality work

CRAFTSMANSHIP

Attention to detail, experienced team, pride in what we do

RELATIONSHIPS

Dependable and positive communication, value our relationship with clients throughout project and after

COMMUNITY

We prioritize supporting the communities we work in through philanthropic efforts with organizations like the Ronald McDonald house

We pride ourselves on creating spaces people love to live in, all while keeping within a budget, designing with quality, and executing with local, experienced craftsmen that

share our values and outlook.

Meet Our Home Remodeling & Renovations Team
CO-OWNERS, STEVE MCDONALD AND ANGELA BARNHART, HAVE A COMBINED 30+ YEARS IN THE DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, AND REAL ESTATE INDUSTRIES.

Bringing this unique combination of experience into each and every project, we guide homeowners through the entire process, from concept to design to construction, to transform their kitchen, bath or lower level space into something they love while also understanding the best options to

maximize their return on investment.

Two stages of remodeling over two years, and now it feels like home. 🤍

Foundry main floor remodel, Lakeville, MN.

#WhiteBirchDesign #LakevilleMN #MainFloorRemodel #KitchenRemodel #MinnesotaHomes

How long does a kitchen remodel actually take? 🏡

For a full remodel, plan on 5 to 7 months from the first conversation to the final walkthrough. 

About half of that time happens before demo day, and that planning is what keeps construction on track.

Swipe through the five phases to see what each one involves and how long it takes. 👉

Thinking about a kitchen project in 2027? Now is the perfect time to start the design conversation. Planning something smaller? We still have a few openings left this year.

📌 Save this for when you’re ready to plan, and reach out through the link in bio. No start date or final design needed, just a conversation.

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #RemodelingTips #designbuildmn 

5 to 7 months covers a full remodel from first conversation to final walkthrough. A cosmetic refresh (new countertops, hardware, paint, and lighting) can move faster. Removing walls or relocating plumbing and electrical puts you toward the longer end.

We start with an initial consultation about your goals, priorities, and general budget range, then a site visit to assess your space and any structural constraints. Early renderings show you what’s possible before anything is decided. This is also where your overall timeline comes into focus.

Showroom visits are one of our favorite parts. Seeing materials in person, side by side and in different light, makes all the difference. Quick deciders move faster, and if you’re still exploring, that’s completely fine. Better to land it here than change course after cabinets are ordered.

Once your contract is signed, we start ordering your selections, many from local Minnesota vendors. Behind the scenes, we’re:
- Placing orders for every selection
- Finalizing permits, if required
- Confirming delivery windows

Many homes built in the ‘90s have closed-off kitchens, half walls, and separate dining rooms, so opening them up often takes structural work. Once walls open, we sometimes find outdated electrical or off-code plumbing. We plan for those surprises and tell you right away when one comes up. Tip: most homeowners set up a temporary kitchen in another room.

The punch list is a detailed walkthrough of everyth

Designed for a family that gathers often, with a main floor that has a place for everyone. 

The character comes from the details. 

Here are nine from this Lakeville main floor remodel: 
1. A stone fireplace up to the existing soffit, under 18-foot ceilings 
2. White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain, with champagne bronze hardware 
3. A custom iron railing from a local ironworker 
4. Tambour on the dining room walls, with sconces 
5. A Tambour wall in the piano room 
6. Tambour on the back of the island, with a Zellige tile backsplash 
7. A custom arched hutch 
8. A powder room gone dark, with wood-textured tile 
9. A cabinet that hides the printer 

Save this one for your own main floor, and see the full project at the link in bio under Kitchen.

#MainFloorRemodel #twincitiesremodeler #LakevilleMN #mndesignbuild #whitebirchdesign 

Start here: a stone fireplace that climbs to the existing soffit under 18-foot ceilings, right at the center of the floor.

White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain and champagne bronze hardware bring warmth to all that stone.

The stairs got a custom iron railing from a local ironworker, and the carpet carries right up beside it.

Take out the soffits and columns, and the dining room opens right up. A Tambour detail brings the texture.

Right across from the dining room, the piano room picks up the same Tambour detail, with sconces on the wall.

Look closely. The Tambour detail follows you into the kitchen on the back of the island, and a Zellige tile backsplash adds more texture.

The custom arched hutch gives this kitchen even more personality.

Then a surprise: the powder room goes dark, with wood-textured tile.

Even the office got a plan: a custom white oak desk and a cabinet that hides the printer. 

Which room is your favorite?

We’re not saying a new kitchen fixes everything. 👀 

We’re just saying nobody has ever been sad about warm white oak cabinets and a custom hood. 🙌 

Fun fact: that hood was finished by a local artisan in a custom color and texture, and it gives the whole room its character. 

First peek at our Foundry Kitchen remodel. Ready to start yours? DM us and let’s talk. 

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #SouthMetroMN #MNDesignBuild

Behind every finished kitchen photo is a lot of nudging, fussing, and “wait, one more inch to the left.” 😄 

Swipe through our latest photo shoot to see what goes into capturing a space the way it deserves: 

🕯️ Finding the perfect placement 
🍏 A little pop of green before the shutter clicks 
📷 Getting every angle just right 
👯 A crew that makes it fun 

The details you live with every day, like the cabinetry, the lighting, and the way a room flows, deserve to be seen properly. That’s why we take the photos as seriously as the build. 

The final reveal is coming soon. 

Thinking about a kitchen, bath, or basement remodel? DM us or tap the link in our bio and let’s talk. 

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #mndesignbuild #twincitiesremodeler

What a whirlwind weekend at R20! Thank you to everyone who stopped by the Parade of Homes Remodelers Showcase. We loved meeting you, hearing about your projects, and answering your questions.

A choppy layout and a few partial walls were boxing in this Lakeville, MN kitchen. Once they came down, it got the room it was always meant to have:

🤍 An island scaled for real life
🤍 A built-in beverage center made for hosting
🤍 Hickory floors running through the whole main level, so it all reads as one space

Missed us, or living with a layout that feels chopped up? Tell us what’s not working. Link in bio to get started.

#remodelersshowcase #ParadeofHomes #twincitiesremodeler #WhiteBirchDesign

Kitchen Remodel Minneapolis MN

Two stages of remodeling over two years, and now it feels like home. 🤍

Foundry main floor remodel, Lakeville, MN.

#WhiteBirchDesign #LakevilleMN #MainFloorRemodel #KitchenRemodel #MinnesotaHomes

How long does a kitchen remodel actually take? 🏡

For a full remodel, plan on 5 to 7 months from the first conversation to the final walkthrough. 

About half of that time happens before demo day, and that planning is what keeps construction on track.

Swipe through the five phases to see what each one involves and how long it takes. 👉

Thinking about a kitchen project in 2027? Now is the perfect time to start the design conversation. Planning something smaller? We still have a few openings left this year.

📌 Save this for when you’re ready to plan, and reach out through the link in bio. No start date or final design needed, just a conversation.

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #RemodelingTips #designbuildmn 

5 to 7 months covers a full remodel from first conversation to final walkthrough. A cosmetic refresh (new countertops, hardware, paint, and lighting) can move faster. Removing walls or relocating plumbing and electrical puts you toward the longer end.

We start with an initial consultation about your goals, priorities, and general budget range, then a site visit to assess your space and any structural constraints. Early renderings show you what’s possible before anything is decided. This is also where your overall timeline comes into focus.

Showroom visits are one of our favorite parts. Seeing materials in person, side by side and in different light, makes all the difference. Quick deciders move faster, and if you’re still exploring, that’s completely fine. Better to land it here than change course after cabinets are ordered.

Once your contract is signed, we start ordering your selections, many from local Minnesota vendors. Behind the scenes, we’re:
- Placing orders for every selection
- Finalizing permits, if required
- Confirming delivery windows

Many homes built in the ‘90s have closed-off kitchens, half walls, and separate dining rooms, so opening them up often takes structural work. Once walls open, we sometimes find outdated electrical or off-code plumbing. We plan for those surprises and tell you right away when one comes up. Tip: most homeowners set up a temporary kitchen in another room.

The punch list is a detailed walkthrough of everyth

Designed for a family that gathers often, with a main floor that has a place for everyone. 

The character comes from the details. 

Here are nine from this Lakeville main floor remodel: 
1. A stone fireplace up to the existing soffit, under 18-foot ceilings 
2. White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain, with champagne bronze hardware 
3. A custom iron railing from a local ironworker 
4. Tambour on the dining room walls, with sconces 
5. A Tambour wall in the piano room 
6. Tambour on the back of the island, with a Zellige tile backsplash 
7. A custom arched hutch 
8. A powder room gone dark, with wood-textured tile 
9. A cabinet that hides the printer 

Save this one for your own main floor, and see the full project at the link in bio under Kitchen.

#MainFloorRemodel #twincitiesremodeler #LakevilleMN #mndesignbuild #whitebirchdesign 

Start here: a stone fireplace that climbs to the existing soffit under 18-foot ceilings, right at the center of the floor.

White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain and champagne bronze hardware bring warmth to all that stone.

The stairs got a custom iron railing from a local ironworker, and the carpet carries right up beside it.

Take out the soffits and columns, and the dining room opens right up. A Tambour detail brings the texture.

Right across from the dining room, the piano room picks up the same Tambour detail, with sconces on the wall.

Look closely. The Tambour detail follows you into the kitchen on the back of the island, and a Zellige tile backsplash adds more texture.

The custom arched hutch gives this kitchen even more personality.

Then a surprise: the powder room goes dark, with wood-textured tile.

Even the office got a plan: a custom white oak desk and a cabinet that hides the printer. 

Which room is your favorite?

We’re not saying a new kitchen fixes everything. 👀 

We’re just saying nobody has ever been sad about warm white oak cabinets and a custom hood. 🙌 

Fun fact: that hood was finished by a local artisan in a custom color and texture, and it gives the whole room its character. 

First peek at our Foundry Kitchen remodel. Ready to start yours? DM us and let’s talk. 

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #SouthMetroMN #MNDesignBuild

Behind every finished kitchen photo is a lot of nudging, fussing, and “wait, one more inch to the left.” 😄 

Swipe through our latest photo shoot to see what goes into capturing a space the way it deserves: 

🕯️ Finding the perfect placement 
🍏 A little pop of green before the shutter clicks 
📷 Getting every angle just right 
👯 A crew that makes it fun 

The details you live with every day, like the cabinetry, the lighting, and the way a room flows, deserve to be seen properly. That’s why we take the photos as seriously as the build. 

The final reveal is coming soon. 

Thinking about a kitchen, bath, or basement remodel? DM us or tap the link in our bio and let’s talk. 

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #mndesignbuild #twincitiesremodeler

What a whirlwind weekend at R20! Thank you to everyone who stopped by the Parade of Homes Remodelers Showcase. We loved meeting you, hearing about your projects, and answering your questions.

A choppy layout and a few partial walls were boxing in this Lakeville, MN kitchen. Once they came down, it got the room it was always meant to have:

🤍 An island scaled for real life
🤍 A built-in beverage center made for hosting
🤍 Hickory floors running through the whole main level, so it all reads as one space

Missed us, or living with a layout that feels chopped up? Tell us what’s not working. Link in bio to get started.

#remodelersshowcase #ParadeofHomes #twincitiesremodeler #WhiteBirchDesign

Two stages of remodeling over two years, and now it feels like home. 🤍

Foundry main floor remodel, Lakeville, MN.

#WhiteBirchDesign #LakevilleMN #MainFloorRemodel #KitchenRemodel #MinnesotaHomes

How long does a kitchen remodel actually take? 🏡

For a full remodel, plan on 5 to 7 months from the first conversation to the final walkthrough. 

About half of that time happens before demo day, and that planning is what keeps construction on track.

Swipe through the five phases to see what each one involves and how long it takes. 👉

Thinking about a kitchen project in 2027? Now is the perfect time to start the design conversation. Planning something smaller? We still have a few openings left this year.

📌 Save this for when you’re ready to plan, and reach out through the link in bio. No start date or final design needed, just a conversation.

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #RemodelingTips #designbuildmn 

5 to 7 months covers a full remodel from first conversation to final walkthrough. A cosmetic refresh (new countertops, hardware, paint, and lighting) can move faster. Removing walls or relocating plumbing and electrical puts you toward the longer end.

We start with an initial consultation about your goals, priorities, and general budget range, then a site visit to assess your space and any structural constraints. Early renderings show you what’s possible before anything is decided. This is also where your overall timeline comes into focus.

Showroom visits are one of our favorite parts. Seeing materials in person, side by side and in different light, makes all the difference. Quick deciders move faster, and if you’re still exploring, that’s completely fine. Better to land it here than change course after cabinets are ordered.

Once your contract is signed, we start ordering your selections, many from local Minnesota vendors. Behind the scenes, we’re:
- Placing orders for every selection
- Finalizing permits, if required
- Confirming delivery windows

Many homes built in the ‘90s have closed-off kitchens, half walls, and separate dining rooms, so opening them up often takes structural work. Once walls open, we sometimes find outdated electrical or off-code plumbing. We plan for those surprises and tell you right away when one comes up. Tip: most homeowners set up a temporary kitchen in another room.

The punch list is a detailed walkthrough of everyth

Designed for a family that gathers often, with a main floor that has a place for everyone. 

The character comes from the details. 

Here are nine from this Lakeville main floor remodel: 
1. A stone fireplace up to the existing soffit, under 18-foot ceilings 
2. White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain, with champagne bronze hardware 
3. A custom iron railing from a local ironworker 
4. Tambour on the dining room walls, with sconces 
5. A Tambour wall in the piano room 
6. Tambour on the back of the island, with a Zellige tile backsplash 
7. A custom arched hutch 
8. A powder room gone dark, with wood-textured tile 
9. A cabinet that hides the printer 

Save this one for your own main floor, and see the full project at the link in bio under Kitchen.

#MainFloorRemodel #twincitiesremodeler #LakevilleMN #mndesignbuild #whitebirchdesign 

Start here: a stone fireplace that climbs to the existing soffit under 18-foot ceilings, right at the center of the floor.

White oak built-ins in a Sandalwood stain and champagne bronze hardware bring warmth to all that stone.

The stairs got a custom iron railing from a local ironworker, and the carpet carries right up beside it.

Take out the soffits and columns, and the dining room opens right up. A Tambour detail brings the texture.

Right across from the dining room, the piano room picks up the same Tambour detail, with sconces on the wall.

Look closely. The Tambour detail follows you into the kitchen on the back of the island, and a Zellige tile backsplash adds more texture.

The custom arched hutch gives this kitchen even more personality.

Then a surprise: the powder room goes dark, with wood-textured tile.

Even the office got a plan: a custom white oak desk and a cabinet that hides the printer. 

Which room is your favorite?

We’re not saying a new kitchen fixes everything. 👀 

We’re just saying nobody has ever been sad about warm white oak cabinets and a custom hood. 🙌 

Fun fact: that hood was finished by a local artisan in a custom color and texture, and it gives the whole room its character. 

First peek at our Foundry Kitchen remodel. Ready to start yours? DM us and let’s talk. 

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #SouthMetroMN #MNDesignBuild

Behind every finished kitchen photo is a lot of nudging, fussing, and “wait, one more inch to the left.” 😄 

Swipe through our latest photo shoot to see what goes into capturing a space the way it deserves: 

🕯️ Finding the perfect placement 
🍏 A little pop of green before the shutter clicks 
📷 Getting every angle just right 
👯 A crew that makes it fun 

The details you live with every day, like the cabinetry, the lighting, and the way a room flows, deserve to be seen properly. That’s why we take the photos as seriously as the build. 

The final reveal is coming soon. 

Thinking about a kitchen, bath, or basement remodel? DM us or tap the link in our bio and let’s talk. 

#WhiteBirchDesign #KitchenRemodel #mndesignbuild #twincitiesremodeler

What a whirlwind weekend at R20! Thank you to everyone who stopped by the Parade of Homes Remodelers Showcase. We loved meeting you, hearing about your projects, and answering your questions.

A choppy layout and a few partial walls were boxing in this Lakeville, MN kitchen. Once they came down, it got the room it was always meant to have:

🤍 An island scaled for real life
🤍 A built-in beverage center made for hosting
🤍 Hickory floors running through the whole main level, so it all reads as one space

Missed us, or living with a layout that feels chopped up? Tell us what’s not working. Link in bio to get started.

Fleur Primary Bath Remodel
This primary bath remodel was an opportunity to completely rethink the space and create a retreat that feels as beautiful as it is functional.

The original bathroom felt closed in and inefficient, with a large corner tub taking up valuable space, a cramped shower, and a layout that didn’t provide the privacy or ease the homeowners needed. A soft, layered color palette brings warmth and depth to the room, balancing deeper cabinetry tones with lighter walls and natural-feeling finishes. Subtle pattern and texture add dimension throughout, while the herringbone tile detail introduces a timeless element and a touch of visual interest.

Every detail was thoughtfully considered to create a space that feels calm, cohesive, and inviting. The result is a primary bath that not only functions beautifully for everyday living, but also feels like a private retreat designed for comfort and relaxation.

Verde Mudroom & Powder Bath Remodel

LAKEVILLE, MN  |  2026

For this busy Lakeville family, the mudroom wasn't just an entryway.
It was the daily landing zone for backpacks, sports gear, shoes, schedules, and everything that comes with an active family life.

Long on the wish list but short on personality and organization, it was finally time to transform this hardworking space into one that felt both beautiful and functional.

A checkerboard floor in warm terracotta and cream was the design spark that started it all. From there, a bold mid-century-inspired palette emerged, anchored by rich Verdant green cabinetry, stained maple shelving, and dark soapstone countertops.

To improve function, the wall between the existing closet and garage entry was removed, creating room for ample storage for everyday essentials including custom shoe storage designed to keep up with the constant rotation of cleats and sneakers. Across the way, a dedicated family command center gives mail, charging stations, calendars, and household clutter a permanent home outside the kitchen.

Personality is layered throughout the space, from Art Deco-inspired palm wallpaper and sculptural brass hardware to playful geometric patterns and rich green accents. In the adjoining powder bath, a hairpin-leg vanity, organic brass lighting, and a celadon green sink continue the home’s collected mid-century aesthetic, proving that even the most practical spaces can make a memorable first impression.

The Nineteenth Hole Primary Bath Remodel

LAKEVILLE, MN  |  2025

Sometimes inspiration shows up in the most unexpected places,
and that's exactly what happened here. A glimpse of Cambria Clovelly in a golf course clubhouse bathroom planted a seed, and a decade-long wish for a primary bath that finally felt personal gave it room to grow.

The original bathroom was dominated by a jetted tub nobody used, a shower that felt undersized, and a layout that lacked privacy and storage. The tub is gone now, replaced by a spacious walk-in shower with a built-in bench and frameless glass enclosure. A dedicated makeup station, better storage, and a reconfigured layout give the space a flow it never had. Meanwhile, seamless aging in place features like shower grab bars, encourage longevity.

The design move that made it all come together was an unconventional one: placing the vanity directly in front of the existing window. Suspended illuminated mirrors and light fixtures hang in front of the glass, preserving views of the outdoors while flooding the space with both natural daylight and warm interior lighting.

As the original source of inspiration, it’s only appropriate that Cambria Clovelly runs throughout, countertops, shower bench, curb, and niche, anchored by rich cherry cabinetry with a dark oak stained finish that ties the bathroom seamlessly to the adjoining suite. Meanwhile, champagne bronze fixtures and textured tile walls add warmth and depth at every turn. The result is a striking, contemporary space that feels personal and completely worth the wait.

Our History
Home 5 About
THE EVOLUTION OF CONSCIENTIOUS HOME REMODELING IN 3 WAVES
3 Generations of Construction Integrity

Not many remodeling firms are recipients of double digit national and regional design awards. Fewer still are able to prove that they have completed 100% of their projects on time and on budget, let alone provide a guaranteed 5-Year workmanship warranty, with regularly scheduled follow-ups. 

Here at Gayler Design Build we point out these accomplishments and client benefits not to boast, but as a natural consequence of our cross-generational, people-centered family values that continue to shape our future.

Founded, family-owned and operated since 1961, Gayler Design Build is located in Danville, CA, and serves the greater Tri-Valley and Lamorinda areas. As a full-service design-build firm, our decades-long success is a result of thorough planning, obsession with quality, and dedication to service excellence. 

What most sets us apart is our focus on you, the homeowner, and clear communication every step of the way. Generations of loyal clients and a steady stream of new customers attest to our friendliness, dependability, and preoccupation with meeting and then exceeding expectations. 

A LONG-STANDING FAMILY LEGACY

Gayler Design Build has been in continuous operation for over six decades, spanning three generations of expert builders. Founded by Chris Gayler’s grandfather, then significantly grown by his parents George and Darlene, our firm continues to flourish steeped in family values. 

George was born and raised in the Bay Area, and started working summers for his dad’s construction business at the age of thirteen. He never looked back, working his way through the ranks, eventually managing what became his own company’s production and sales departments.

A year after getting his contractor’s license in 1979, George officially took over the firm and expanded the company’s service offerings to include commercial and residential design-build work. His expertise gave him a deep understanding of what makes a project successful. 

From these experiences and insights, George created the unique and proprietary Gayler Process—a highly efficient design-build system that has resulted in award-winning projects, and an unmatched 23-year consistent record of on-time, on-budget construction project delivery. This process evolved and improved with Darlene’s business acumen and natural ability to foster client relationships when she joined the company in 2000. 

“It’s not uncommon for some contractors to provide an unrealistic cost estimate simply to get the business,” says George, shaking his head. “But we understood early on that trust is based on full transparency and consistently doing what you say you’re going to do. So, at Gayler Design Build we go to great lengths to provide accurate fixed cost budget estimates in timeframes that we work fervently to keep.”

George and Darlene also saw the value of hiring and working with a close, cohesive team of talented designers and architects on every project. By seamlessly connecting the design and construction phases of each project, working in close collaboration with the homeowner, we devised unique creative solutions that not only saves our clients money, but delivers faster and more accurately. 

 

A HEARTFELT COMMITMENT TO CULTURE AND VALUES

In January 2020, George was thrilled to pass the family business to his son Chris, A graduate of UC Santa Barbara, Chris has worn many hats at Gayler since 2003. He now applies his contractor’s license, communications degree, and tech background to help the firm thrive.

 

“I grew up within this warm and loving family,” beams Chris, “and that’s meant the world to me. So every day I strive to make everyone I interact with feel similarly at home. We’re all human, full of strengths and weaknesses. It’s important to treat everyone with dignity and respect.”

With family central to everything they do, the Gaylers consider everyone within their circle part of their family, too. From their architects and interior designers to craftspeople, carpenters, and office staff, and especially to their loyal customers, they treat people like their own. 

A WORKPLACE ALLEGIANCE TO COMMUNITY

The Gaylers apply that philosophy throughout the community, too. In addition to hiring veterans and volunteering for numerous charity projects, the company donates money and resources to extraordinary causes that fuel their clients’ dedication and passion. 

Deeply rooted in the community, Chris, in particular, serves on the boards of the San Ramon Rotary, Valley Education Foundation, and is a graduate of the San Ramon Leadership program. His wife, Natalie, is also dedicated to our school district, and teaches ESL at Live Oak Elementary.

Sweethearts since love at first sight, Chris and Natalie have created a beautiful family of their own, raising two spirited and good-natured young men; Ethan and Zachary. The family enjoys sports, rooting for the Giants, and exploring the great outdoors with their labrador retriever.

“I don’t draw any lines between business ethics and community service,” says Chris. “Our clients, after all, are also our neighbors. So our job is to not only bring joy to every design-build project, but apply that same spirit to helping our entire community thrive.” 

Proving his point, George set the standard with company mission and values. The result of treating people with respect and like their own extended family speaks for itself, showcasing a company legacy that offers extreme value, unmatched quality, and proven performance:

Value
Reliable—Every project, on time and on budget since 1999
Trusted—Five-year workmanship warranty (5 x’s the one-year industry standard)
Efficient—By seamlessly connecting the design and construction phases of each project, working in close collaboration with the homeowner, we devised unique creative solutions that not only saves our clients money, but delivers faster and more accurately.
Care—Treated like family, by family  
Quality
22 national and regional design and craftsmanship awards
Named Remodeling Magazine’s Top 50 national remodeling firms
Voted #1 remodeling contractor in the Danville Weekly/Express multiple years
Performance

Family owned and founded in 1961—serving Tri-Valley and Lamorind areas over 6 decades 
Referrals from past clients account for 60% of our business
125 years of combined management experience
35% shorter project durations than the industry average
4 licensed contractors in a single firm
26.7 years of experience, on average, for our trades

INCEPTION

1980

2015

2022

“When people ask me how Gayler Design Build is different,” smiles Chris, “I say there’s a whole lot to be said with a perfect track record of over twenty-three years. At the end of the day, clients want up front honesty, and every job done right and on time, as promised.”
VISION FOR FUTURE

“I’m privileged and honored to walk in my father’s footsteps, who walked in his own father’s before that,” says Chris. “One of the most important lessons they taught me is to leave things in an even better shape than when you found them. And that’s exactly what I will do here.”

To meet that goal, Chris is seamlessly continuing his family legacy of honest estimates, award-winning quality, and expectation-exceeding customer service. He sees the future of Gayler Design Build as one of steady growth, satisfied staff and clients, and superb work. 

“We’ve been in business for over six decades,” adds Chris. “I just want people who hear the name Gayler Design Build six decades from now to similarly know that we remain all about integrity, quality, longevity, and a great company with a great family still at the helm.”

Our Philosophy
Home 5 About 5 Our Philosophy
WHAT WE DO

We design and remodel kitchens, baths, whole houses, and outdoor living spaces, as well as design and build additions, doing so with superior efficiency, quality craftsmanship, dependable communication, and family-like, personalized attention.

k
Our Mission

We are the remodeler of choice in the Tri-Valley area for homeowners who appreciate the extraordinary design/build experience, and demand the highest quality and craftsmanship.


Our Vision

We are the most sought after, and highly respected design-build remodeling company in the Tri-Valley and Lamorinda areas, providing remodeling and design services to homeowners in Alamo, San Ramon, Danville, Diablo, Pleasanton, Livermore, Walnut Creek, Lafayette, Orinda, Moraga, and Dublin.


Our Values

Our values are our business ethics. They reflect what is truly important to us, guiding how we make decisions between ourselves, our clients, partners, and the public in general. These values may not be compromised. They are absolute and define who we are, how we work, and what we believe in.

“We can see why Gayler Design Build has been in business for over 50 years – integrity, pride in work, honor, commitment, courtesy, professionalism, and support of local business and the community. We will definitely use them for any future projects and will continue to recommend them to local friends and family.”

— Lani and John A. , San Danville, CA

OUR BUSINESS VALUES ARE:

 

Our Team: We take great pride in what we do, and treat everyone with fairness and respect.
Our Focus: We get the job done through teamwork, organization, and attention to detail.
Results: We are accountable to those we serve, and consistently produce reliable, high quality, and on-time results.
Communication: We communicate clearly, directly, honestly, and in a timely manner.
Credibility: We are highly credible because we are honest, loyal, and reliable.
Enjoyment: We enjoy what we do, have fun doing it, and take great pride in our work.
Personal Growth: We continually grow in our profession and craft, and provide an environment that supports that growth.
Leadership: We produce reliable results through structure, process, and teamwork.
Appreciation: We consistently express our gratitude and appreciation to our clients, partners, and staff.

HELPING BUILD A STRONG COMMUNITY

Strengthening the local community that we serve is fundamental to the success of our business. It’s what grounds us and makes us feel a part of something greater than ourselves.

From our inception, it has been our great privilege to donate our time and resources to the extraordinary causes that fuel our clients’ dedication and passion. Here are a few of those local charities/organizations:

LEARN MORE
Building Robots, Building Futures

We’re proud to support the Cookie Bots, the Girl Scout troop we sponsored in the NorCal Championships STEM robotics competition! These girls had an amazing experience, and now they’re paying it forward—teaching robotics workshops to inspire younger girls in STEM! With competition season behind them, they’re already brainstorming new strategies for next year. We love seeing young minds innovate, learn, and lead! Way to go, Cookie Bots!

LEARN MORE
I Can Do That! Performing Arts Center

Gayler Design Build is proud to support ICDT! (I Can Do That!), a vibrant local nonprofit theatre company based in Danville. Since opening the doors to its stunning Performing Arts Center in 2021, ICDT! has been inspiring young performers through acting, singing, and dancing. But it’s more than just the arts—it’s about building confidence, connection, and a strong sense of community. We love being part of a mission that helps kids shine on stage and in life.

LEARN MORE
Alamo Women’s Club, Authors’ Faire Program

Supporting Local Women, Education & Community Impact

Gayler Design Build is proud to sponsor the Alamo Women’s Club, a dynamic group of 100 women from across the East Bay who have been serving the community since 1916. The club focuses on philanthropy, education, and local engagement—awarding 70+ need-based scholarships over the past eight years and raising funds through events like the annual Authors’ Faire, held at the Blackhawk Museum and attended by over 300 guests.

Our sponsorship helps fuel their mission to uplift those in need, invest in future leaders, and build a stronger community for all.

LEARN MORE
Fostering Wishes

Fostering Wishes is dedicated to improving the lives of children in foster care, and empowers them for a self-sufficient future. Join us in supporting our 1st Annual Fostering Wishes holiday gift drive.

LEARN MORE
White Pony Express

Another cause near and dear to our heart is the importance of protecting our planet and nourishing our community. That’s why Gayler Design Build supports White Pony Express whose mission is to eliminate hunger and poverty by delivering the abundance all around us to those in need. Their services are provided free of charge and operated mostly by volunteers, providing food and clothing, toys, books, and more.

LEARN MORE
Toys For Tots

The Marine Toys for Tots Program has been delivering a message of hope to less fortunate youngsters since 1947. Its program started to collect and distribute new, unwrapped toys to children in need at Christmas. It has since evolved to to be diligently altruistic in providing joy and books to children in need across America, no matter the season. Gayler Design Build proudly supports this organization each year.

LEARN MORE
Discovery Counseling Center
of the San Ramon Valley, Inc.

Counseling can facilitate change and bring hope. Fortunately, this is the Discovery Counseling Center’s mantra. Its mission is to provide high quality, accessible and affordable mental wellness services to San Ramon Valley. In support of this desperately needed service, Gayler Design Build actively contributes to the Endowment Fund on a monthly basis.

LEARN MORE
Lazarex Cancer Foundation

The vision of Lazarex Cancer Foundation is that everyone affected by cancer will have hope, dignity, support and the most advanced treatments made available to them at all stages of their journey. This fabulous cancer foundation located in Danville, CA accepts monthly giving that allows for the planned growth of a number of patients they will financially assist. Gayler Design Build has set up a recurring gift option on a monthly basis to #GIVEHOPE.

LEARN MORE
San Ramon Valley Education Foundation

The San Ramon Valley Education Foundation is the primary fundraising organization working in partnership with the San Ramon Valley Unified School District to provide financial support and promote public education in our community. Donations directly impact children among each of the thirty-six elementary, middle, and high schools within the San Ramon Valley Unified School District.

Gayler Design Build is proud to be a long-time supporter of this organization, advocating and promoting public education. Thank you for helping us support our local schools.

LEARN MORE
Taylor Family Foundation

The Taylor Family Foundation’s mission is to preserve the wellness and enhance the quality of life for children in Northern California living with life-threatening and chronic illnesses, developmental disabilities and youth at-risk through unique therapeutic experiences and support. We became involved with the Taylor Family Foundation through our dear friends, Elaine Taylor and her late husband, Barry.

LEARN MORE
Students Rising Above

The Students Rising Above community is dedicated to impacting the future through the cultivation of extraordinary youth. SRA invests in low-income, first-generation college students who have demonstrated a deep commitment to education and strength of character while overcoming tremendous odds of poverty, homelessness, and neglect. They help each student to realize his or her potential by guiding and supporting them through college graduation, and into the workforce.

Gayler Design Build is proud to support a local organization that helps its graduates break the cycle of poverty within their own families, serve their communities, provide a new generation of employees and leaders from diverse backgrounds, and accelerate positive change.

LEARN MORE
Wounded Warrior Project

Wounded Warrior Project® (WWP) serves veterans and service members who incurred a physical or mental injury, illness or wound, co-incident to their military service on or after September 11, 2001 and their families.

Gayler Design Build is proud to honor and empower Wounded Warriors.

LEARN MORE
CPI Foundation

The CPI Foundation partners with the U.S. Departments of Defense and Interior, and with industry companies across the country who support their programs and hire their alumni.

They benefit the United States and its taxpayers by combining the strengths and needs of three national concerns: our military veterans, our infrastructure, and our national parks. Helping avoid potential military-to-civilian transition pitfalls, they offer career preparation, nationwide placement, & hands-on training for transitioning active duty service members at all levels from all service branches while completing construction, repair, & safety/access projects in national parks.

Gayler Design Build is partnering with the CPI Foundation for the first time in 2022, giving hands-on carpentry training to an active duty service member that we’re excited to support.

LEARN MORE
Contra Costa County Food Bank

Started in 1975, the Food Bank of Contra Costa and Solano stores and distributes donated and purchased perishable and nonperishable food items. We distribute food directly to low-income people at community sites and make food available for other nonprofit organizations serving the ill, needy, and children.

Gayler Design Build supports the Food Bank, which works to reduce food waste, feed hungry people and raise public awareness of issues related to food and hunger.

LEARN MORE
St. Jude’s

St. Jude is leading the way the world understands, treats, and defeats childhood cancer and other life-threatening diseases.

Gayler Design Build is pleased to be able to support the hospital’s mission to advance cures, and means of prevention, for pediatric catastrophic diseases through research and treatment.

Demonstrate how sustainable lifestyles and responsible operations are financially advantageous to our community.

AWARDS

Over the years, Gayler Design Build has been recognized for superior design, exquisite quality craftsmanship, and outstanding service. Here is a listing of our local, regional and national awards.

2026 Nextdoor Fave Award Winner – General Contractor

 

Gayler Design Build was named a 2026 Nextdoor Fave Award Winner in the General Contractor category as part of Nextdoor’s 10th Annual Local Business Awards. This recognition is especially meaningful because winners are selected through votes and recommendations from local neighbors, reflecting the trust and support of the communities we serve.

2023–2026 Guildmaster with Highest Distinction Award Recipient​ 

Gayler Design Build has earned GuildQuality’s Guildmaster with Highest Distinction Award for four consecutive years (2023–2026), a reflection of its ongoing commitment to delivering an exceptional client experience.

Each year, this honor is awarded to a select group of residential construction professionals who achieve a recommendation rate of 90% or higher, based on verified customer survey responses. Chosen from nearly 2,000 eligible companies nationwide, Gayler Design Build continues to stand among the industry’s top performers, demonstrating a consistent dedication to quality, communication, and client satisfaction.
